This is typically the first step in any tabletop RPG or D&D-styled game. Use your imagination to think up what type of character you want to be in this world. Make sure it remains mostly thematic regarding the setting, as this isn't a standard D&D campaign.

Think about what race you would like your character to be, their personality, goals, back story, specialties, career, appearance, traits, and relationships. Once you have all of these qualities decided, start following the steps below and writing everything down.

Using a "Character Sheet" provided by Wizards of the Coast for 5th Edition, you can track much of this. You may need to make a few modifications for certain things, like tracking your Domain Expansion.

Races in the Jujutsu Kaisen world are quite limited, mostly being between cursed spirits and humans. Deciding your race can be pretty important to describing your character's appearance and abilities, as well as occasionally defining their goals. Humans are easily the most common race to find when exploring the planet, Curses however are peculiar and in all shapes and sizes and limited to mostly Japan although rarely found outside. More information on these races is listed in Chapter 2.

Each character should specialize in a field while killing cursed spirits. A class will determine your prominent talents and skills, allowing your character to hone and grow their abilities throughout the adventure. For example, a brawler may focus mainly on fighting while a strategist can be useful in performing specific tasks outside of combat that may benefit the group, such as curtains. While having an all-around useful character is important, sometimes it doesn't hurt to have a character that tends to be extremely good at only one thing, so long as they benefit the group and feel fun to play. A well-rounded party can make the journey far more enjoyable in the long run.

Put some time into deciding what you want your character's role to be in the unit. Maybe discuss it with others in the group to see what would work best for everyone. However, make sure to choose something you will have fun with and appreciate. Once you have a general idea of what your class will be, pick from the classes listed in Chapter 3.

First, hopefully, you've already decided on a name for your character. If not, try to think of something you like the sound of. If you can't think of anything, feel free to look up D&D name generators online. Then, start to develop their personality and appearance in your head.

After you have a concept in mind, you want to start writing and organizing these ideas onto your character sheet. Try to find what Alignment best fits them and their morals. Then, start to think up some defining Personality Traits. Once you mark those down on your character sheet, start getting into their Ideals, Bonds, and Flaws. These will provide a guideline on how you plan on roleplaying and making decisions with your character.

Now you want to decide on your character's Background. Your background will provide you with tools and knowledge gained from how you've lived your life before the start of the campaign. This will affect how those who recognize you interact with you, how you're treated by the general public, and what your occupation is or was. A DM may provide you with custom backgrounds for this adventure, but feel free to choose from the ones listed in Chapter 4.

By exploring the World and fighting your way through various forces, your characters will start to develop new strategies and grow stronger over time. Each time a major advancement occurs, either due to reaching a specific number of Experience Points or reaching a Milestone in the story, you will gain a Character Level.

For example, if you start at level 1 with 0 Experience Points and gain enough experience throughout a session to make your way to Level 2, you will mark this on your character sheet and upgrade your stats accordingly during your next Long Rest. Additionally, your DM may decide to use a Milestone system by granting you a level up upon reaching a new area or island, completing an important objective, or obtaining a key item or treasure.
While many humans vary in shape and size, your human character will have these traits.
One ability score of your choice increases by 2 and other ability scores increase by 1. Choosing different Human races replaces this ASI.
Humans reach adulthood in their teens and live for around a century.
There is no clear alignment that is consistent among all humans. Just about any alignment can be justified.
Humans in the Jujutsu Kaisen world are typically 5-6 feet tall. Some can rest far outside this range, but your size will count as medium.
Your base walking speed is 30 feet.
You are part of a family of sorcerers or have been involved from a young age, you gain the following:
One ability score of your choice increases by 2 and another by 1.
You gain proficiency in martial weapons.
You gain a Cursed Energy feat.

Very rarely, some humans may be astonishingly stronger than most others in the world, sometimes vastly stronger than the average human. If your human character happens to fall under this category, you can choose to replace the standard Human Ability Score Increase with these traits instead:
You increase either your Strength, Dexterity, or Constitution score by 2 and the others by 1.
You have proficiency in the Athletics skill, if you already have proficiency, you instead gain Expertise.

You can focus on occasionally shrugging off injury. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to roll a d12. Add your Constitution modifier to the number rolled, and reduce the damage by that total. After you use this trait, you can’t use it again until you finish a short or long rest.
You count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift.
Sorcerers who became cursed objects, and are now in a new body
Your lifespan depends on the body you have possessed.
Cursed vessels are almost always chaotic people, not caring about what happens to others around them and wanting to cause destruction.
Your size depends on the race you have possessed.
. Your base walking speed depends on the race you have possessed.
You have advantage on saving throws against effects that would alter or change your form.
You can speak, read, and write Common and one other language of your choice.

There are multiple forms of vessels, however they are all based on consuming cursed objects. There are the reincarnated, who were simply sorcerers who were consumed by creatures who were adapted for their incarnation. There are the death paintings, which take over the body of said vessel despite its host having a will. And then there are the incomplete and complete vessels. In case the cursed object's host still had a will, it would start as an incomplete vessel and then become a complete vessel after erasing the will of the old body owner.
You are a sorcerer from a past era. Now you are in your second life through some deal or accident.
You have been brought back to your peak, you can choose one ability score to increase by 2 and another ability score to increase by 2.
This isn't your first shot at life and last time you learned a few things. You will gain proficiency in two skills or one skill and one tool of your choice.
You have died once and refuse to let it happen again. Whenever you are reduced to 0 hit points, you can choose to instead remain at 1 hit point, once per
A disastrous mixture of curse and man made by an evil scientist. Stuck as a fetus until fed to a host.
Your cursed object has overcome the body of your initial host, so instead of gaining the host's ability scores, you gain a +3 to your Cursed Energy score. This cannot go above 20.
Once you incarnated into a vessel, due to your unnatural properties the body became more durable. Your maximum hit points increase by 2, and increase by 2 again every time you gain a level.

Your birth came from someone from the Kamo clan, and from experimentation, your blood became poisonous. As a reaction, when you take piercing or slashing damage, you can choose a creature within 5 feet of you to take poison damage equal to your proficiency bonus. If the creature has an injury or less than their maximum hit points, they must make a DC 10 Constitution save or be poisoned until the end
Beings made of cursed energy within a shell, somehow gaining sentience.
You increase one ability score of your choice by 4, as you are purpose built for a single purpose.
Your lifespan is hypothetically infinite if you repair yourself.
Cursed Corpses are almost always neutral people, not caring about what happens to others around them and usually wanting to exist peacefully.
Your size can be small to large.
Your base walking speed is 35 feet.
As a construct, you don’t need to breathe, drink, eat, or sleep. However you need materials to mend yourself during a rest.
You can speak, read, and write Common
There are multiple forms of corpses. The soft bodies range from plush like, to normal living materials like flesh. Hard Shell is
the hard skinned stone, wood, or metal.
The simpler, more life-like Cursed Corpses are soft bodies, with their life-like design having both advantages and flaws.
You gain expertise in either intimidation, persuasion, or performance.

You can make a Performance check to disguise yourself as what you resemble. Your sudden reveal may stun an enemy. Once per long rest when you reveal yourself, you can force a creature within 10 feet to make a Wisdom saving throw:
the beginning of their turn on failure.
The more complicated intricate form of Cursed Corpses are the hard shells. Their combat ability is not to be underestimated.
Your body has built-in defensive layers, which can be enhanced with armor.
You gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class.

You can don only armor with which you have proficiency. To don armor, you must incorporate it into your body over the course of 1 hour, during which you must remain in contact with the armor. To doff armor, you must spend 1 hour removing it. You can rest while donning or doffing armor in this way.
While you live, your armor can't be removed from your body against your will.
Beings made up of negative energy, festering over time.
You increase one ability score of your choice by 2 and another by 1.
You are cursed to live forever.
Cursed Spirits rarely maintain any level of intelligence, but when they do, their alignment turns towards being more Chaotic or Evil.
Your size can be Small or Medium.
Your base walking speed is 30 feet.
. You function completely differently from normal creatures:
You don’t need to eat, drink, breathe or sleep, but must remain inactive for 4 hours a day to gain the benefits of a long rest.
You have advantage on saving throws against disease and being poisoned, and you have resistance to poison damage.
You are immune to nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing, or slashing.
You are invisible to creatures without cursed energy.

. Due to your nature of being made of cursed energy, you are unable to utilize reverse cursed technique which is positive energy. Though you can still restore your body with pure cursed energy. Starting at 5th level, you can spend cursed energy up to your CE modifier to regain 5 hit points per cursed energy spent as an action once per turn.
. There are several types of cursed spirits, depending on your origin.
You were once human, but when you died your powerful grudge made you into a curse.
. When reduced to 0 hit points, you can choose to remain at 1 hit point. You can use this feature once per long rest.
. When you choose this subrace, choose a race that you hated. You gain a +2 bonus to damage rolls against that race.
You are made up of humanity’s fears, formed from a shared negative image.

. As an action, you can force all creatures within 30 feet of you to make a Wisdom saving throw against your Cursed Energy save DC. On a failure, they are frightened of you for 1 minute. A creature can repeat the save at the end of their turn. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you finish a long rest.
. You gain proficiency in Intimidation and have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls against frightened creatures.
Plague and sickness are concepts cursed by humanity, giving rise to powerful curses.
. You are immune to disease and poison, as well as the poisoned condition. Your unarmed strikes deal 1d4 poison damage on a hit.

. As an action, you can force all creatures within 30 feet of you to make a Constitution saving throw against your Cursed Energy save DC. On a failure, they gain the poisoned condition for 1 minute. A creature can repeat this save at the end of their turn. Once you use this feature, you cannot use it again until you complete a long rest.
You are a young cursed spirit that has yet to develop.
. Your AC equals 14 + your Constitution modifier while not wearing armor.
. Your hit point maximum increases by an amount equal to your level and increases by 1 whenever you gain a level.

1d12 (or 7) + your Constitution modifier per Juggernaut level after 1st
Choose two from Animal Handling, Athletics, Intimidation, Nature, Perception, and Survival
You start with the following equipment, in addition to the equipment granted by your background:
(a) a greataxe or (b) any martial melee weapon
(a) two handaxes or (b) any simple weapon
An explorer's pack and four javelins

Starting at 1st level, you were born with an Innate Technique. Innate Techniques are unique abilities congenitally engraved into the user's body, specifically in the right prefrontal cortex of the brain. Most jujutsu sorcerers are born with an innate technique that manifests around the age of five or six, which continually carves its formula into the user over time. You must choose one Innate Technique, all detailed under Innate Techniques. Your choice grants you features at 1st, and again at 3rd, 6th, 11th, and 18th level.

At 1st level, your life of scrapping and battling with beasts, has given you mastery of Combat styles that use unarmed strikes and Juggernaut weapons, which are melee weapons without the two-handed property, and improvised weapons. You can not use the finesse property of a weapon while using it as a Juggernaut weapon.
You can roll a d6 in place of the normal damage of your unarmed strike or Juggernaut weapon. This die changes as you gain Juggernaut levels, as shown in the scrapper column on the Juggernaut table.

When you use the Attack action with an unarmed strike or a Juggernaut weapon on your turn, you can make one unarmed strike or grapple as a bonus action. For example, if you take the Attack action and Attack with a Club, you can also make an Unarmed Strike or grapple as a Bonus Action, assuming you haven’t already taken a Bonus Action this turn.
While you are not wearing any armor and not using a shield, your Armor Class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Constitution modifier.
At 2nd level, in battle, you fight with an unstoppable focus. On your turn, you can enter a focus as a bonus action. While focused, you gain the following benefits while not wearing heavy armor:
You have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws.
You have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage.
You add your proficiency bonus to Strength based melee damage rolls.

Your focus lasts for 1 minute. It ends early if you are knocked unconscious. You can also end your focus on your turn as a bonus action. You can focus a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus each long rest.

Starting at 2nd level, you can throw aside all concern for defense to attack with fierce desperation. When you make your first attack on your turn, you can decide to attack recklessly. Doing so gives you advantage on melee weapon attack rolls using Strength during this turn, but attack rolls against you have advantage until your next turn.

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. You can also ignore this increase to instead gain a Feat.
Beginning at 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
Starting at 5th level, as part of your bonus action while entering a focus, you can move up to half your movement speed towards an enemy.
By 7th level, your instincts are so honed that you have advantage on initiative rolls.

Additionally, if you are surprised at the beginning of combat and aren't incapacitated, you can act normally on your first turn, but only if you enter your focus before doing anything else on that turn.
Beginning at 9th level, you can roll one additional weapon damage die when determining the extra damage for a critical hit with a melee attack.
This increases to two additional dice at 13th level and three additional dice at 17th level.

Starting at 10th level, your focus can keep you fighting despite grievous wounds. If you drop to 0 hit points while you're focused and don't die outright, you can make a DC 10 Constitution saving throw. If you succeed, you drop to 1 hit point instead.
Each time you use this feature after the first, the DC increases by 5. When you finish a short or long rest, the DC resets to 10.
Beginning at 14th level, you also gain resistance to necrotic damage while focused.
Beginning at 15th level, your focus is so fierce that it only ends if you fall unconscious or if you choose to end it.
At 20th level, you are aware of your role in society and will do your best to fulfill it. Your Strength and Constitution scores increase by
4. Your maximum for those scores is now 24.

1d8 (or 5) + your Constitution modifier per scout level after 1st
Simple weapons, handguns, longswords, rapiers, and shortswords

(a) a shortbow and quiver of 20 arrows or (b) a shortsword
(a) a burglar's pack, (b) dungeoneer's pack, or (c) an explorer's pack
Dense coat, two daggers, and thieves' tools

Starting at 1st level, you were born with an Innate Technique. Innate Techniques are unique abilities congenitally engraved into the user's body, specifically in the right prefrontal cortex of the brain. Most jujutsu sorcerers are born with an innate technique that manifests around the age of five or six, which continually carves its formula into the user over time. You must choose one Innate Technique, all detailed under Innate Techniques. Your choice grants you features at 1st, and again at 3rd, 6th, 11th, and 18th level.

At 1st level, your practice of martial arts gives you mastery of combat styles that use unarmed strikes and scout weapons, which are shortswords and any simple melee weapons that don't have two-handed or heavy properties.
You can use Dexterity instead of Strength for the attack and damage rolls of your unarmed strikes and scout weapons.
You can roll a d4 in place of the normal damage of your unarmed strike or scout weapon. This die changes as you gain scout levels, as shown in the damage dice column of the Scout table.

When you use the Attack action with an unarmed strike or a scout weapon on your turn, you can make one unarmed strike as a bonus action. For example, if you take the Attack action and attack with a quarterstaff, you can also make an unarmed strike as a bonus action, assuming you haven't already taken a bonus action this turn.
At 1st level, your speed increases by 10 feet. This bonus increases when you reach certain scout levels, as shown in the scout table
At 9th level, you gain the ability to move along vertical surfaces and across liquids on your turn without falling during the move.
Starting at 2nd level, your quick thinking and agility allow you to move and act quickly. You can take the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action as a bonus action.

At 2nd level, you can make a bonus action Insight check against your opponents against an opponent’s Deception check. On a success, you gain an advantage on all rolls against that opponent for that turn.

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. You can also ignore this increase to instead gain a Feat.
Starting at 5th level, you can see even fine details up to a mile away. You also gain advantage on Perception checks using sight.
At 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of once when you use the Attack action during your turn.

Beginning at 7th level, you can nimbly dodge out of the way of certain area effects, such as a red dragon's fiery breath or an Ice Storm technique. When you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you instead take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, and only half damage if you fail. At 15th level, you can choose a second saving throw and gain the same effects from it.
At 10th level, if an opponent moves within 5ft of you, you can move up to your movement speed as a reaction.
When you reach 15th level, you can move up to twice your speed.
Beginning at 13th level, you can now as a part of
tell your opponent's weaknesses(Weak Points, Vulnerabilities) and main attacks (Damage Type and highest damage action).
Beginning at 14th level, you gain advantage on Dexterity saving throws and blindsight out to 30 feet.

Starting at 17th level, when an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to ignore the attack's damage against you. You can use this feature a number of times equal to half your proficiency bonus (rounded up) per long rest.
Beginning at 20th level, your speed is faster than anyone can track. Your movement becomes instant and cannot provoke opportunity attacks.
Innate Technique Feature, Ability Score Improvement
1d6 (or 4) + your Constitution modifier per strategist level after 1st
Daggers, darts, slings, quarterstaffs, and handguns
Choose two from Arcana, History, Insight, Investigation, Medicine, and Religion
(a) a component pouch or (b) an arcane focus
(a) a scholar's pack or (b) an explorer's pack

Starting at 1st level, you were born with an Innate Technique. Innate Techniques are unique abilities congenitally engraved into the user's body, specifically in the right prefrontal cortex of the brain. Most jujutsu sorcerers are born with an innate technique that manifests around the age of five or six, which continually carves its formula
into the user over time. You must choose one Innate Technique, all detailed under Innate Techniques. Your choice grants you features at 1st, and again at 3rd, 6th, 11th, and 18th levels.
You have a pool of latent cursed energy that replenishes when you take a long rest. The pool equals half your Strategist level (rounded up) and you can draw from it at will.
For example, if you're a 4th-level strategist, you have a pool of 2 cursed energy points. You can recover either 1 at two different times or 2 at once.
At 2nd level, you gain the ability to twist cursed techniques to suit your needs. You gain two of the following Modification options of your choice. You gain another one at 10th and 17th levels.
You can use only one Modification option on a technique when you cast it unless otherwise specified.

When you cast a technique that forces other creatures to make a saving throw, you can protect some of those creatures from the technique's full force. To do so, you spend 1 cursed energy and choose a number of those creatures up to your Cursed Energy modifier (minimum of one). A chosen creature automatically succeeds on its saving throw against the technique.

When you cast a technique that has a range of 5 feet or greater, you can spend 1 cursed energy to double the range of the technique. When you cast a technique that has a range of touch, you can spend 1 cursed energy to make the range of the technique 30 feet.

When you roll damage for a technique, you can spend 1 cursed energy to reroll a number of the damage dice up to your Cursed Energy modifier (minimum of one). You must use the new rolls. You can use Empowered technique even if you have already used a different Modification option.
When you cast a technique that has a duration of 1 minute or longer, you can spend 1 cursed energy to double its duration, to a maximum duration of 24 hours.

When you cast a technique that forces a creature to make a saving throw to resist its effects, you can spend 3 cursed energy to give one target of the technique disadvantage on its first saving throw against the technique.
When you cast a technique that has a casting time of 1 action, you can spend 2 cursed energy to change the casting time to 1 bonus action for this casting.

If you make an attack roll for a technique and miss, you can spend 2 cursed energy to reroll the d20, and you must use the new roll. You can use Seeking technique even if you have already used a different Modification option.
When you cast a technique, you can spend 1 cursed energy to cast it without somatic or verbal components.

When you cast a technique that deals a type of damage from the following list, you can spend 1 cursed energy to change that damage type to one of the other listed types: acid, cold, fire, lightning, poison, or thunder.

a technique that targets only one creature and doesn't have a range of self, you can spend a number of cursed energy equal to the technique's cost to target a second creature in range with the same technique (1 cursed energy if the technique is free). To be eligible, a technique must be incapable of targeting more than one creature at the technique's current level.

When you reach 4th level, and again at 6th, 8th, 10th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. You can also ignore this increase to instead gain a Feat.
At 15th level, you regain 4 cursed energy on a short rest.

At 20th level, you can choose a feature that uses cursed energy, that is not a domain expansion, maximum, or reverse curse technique, and use it for no cursed energy cost. It counts as the minimum input of Cursed Energy necessary.

1d8 (or 5) + your Constitution modifier per shikigami user level
Daggers, darts, slings, quarterstaffs, and handguns

Starting at 1st level, you were born with an Innate Technique. Innate Techniques are unique abilities congenitally engraved into the user's body, specifically in the right prefrontal cortex of the brain. Most jujutsu sorcerers are born with an innate technique that manifests around the age of five or six, which continually carves its formula into the user over time. You must choose one Innate Technique, all detailed under Innate Techniques. Your choice grants you features at 1st, and again at 3rd, 6th, 11th, and 18th levels.

Beginning at 1st level, you shape your cursed energy into a living being under your control and determine its appearance. As an action, you can summon the shikigami that is bound to you. It appears in an unoccupied space of your choice within 30 feet of you. You can summon your shikigami companion for free once per long rest or again as an action for 3 cursed energy.

The shikigami is friendly to you and your companions, and it obeys your commands. Use its game statistics in the accompanying Shikigami Companion stat blocks, which uses your proficiency bonus (PB) in several places.

In combat, the shikigami shares your initiative and takes its turn immediately after yours. It can move and use its reaction on its own, but only takes the Dodge action unless you take a bonus action on your turn to command it to take another action. That action can be one in its statblock or some other action. If you are incapacitated, the shikigami can take any action of its choice, not just Dodge.
The shikigami remains until reduced to 0 hit points, you summon the shikigami again, or you die. Anything the shikigami was wearing or carrying is left behind when it vanishes.

At 1st level, your practice of martial arts gives you mastery of combat styles that use unarmed strikes, shortswords and any simple melee weapons that lack the two-handed or heavy property. You gain the following benefits while unarmed or wielding a Martial Arts Weapons:
You can use Dexterity instead of Strength for attack and damage rolls of your unarmed strikes and martial arts weapons.

You can roll a d4 in place of the normal damage of your unarmed strike or martial arts weapon. This die changes as you gain shikigami user levels, as shown in the Martial Arts column of the shikigami user table.

When you use the Attack action with an unarmed strike or a Martial Arts weapon on your turn, you can make one unarmed strike as a bonus action. For example, if you take the Attack action and attack with a quarterstaff, you can also make an unarmed strike as a bonus action, if you haven't already taken a bonus action.

At 2nd level, your attunement with your shikigami has increased. Any effects or actions granted to you by your technique are also granted to your Shikigami Companion (other than summons), drawing from your pool of CE.

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1 for both you and your shikigami companion (max of 20) or instead gain a feat.
Beginning at 5th level, you and your shikigami strike as one. As part of the attack action, you can
command your companion to move and attack a creature within range or take a different action.
Starting at 7th level, your shikigami grows stronger. Your companion gains the following:
It gains a hover speed equal to its walking speed
Its strike attacks deal 1d6 extra necrotic damage
You can either choose for your shikigami to become medium or gain the ability to become any weapon, dealing an additional 1d6 necrotic damage on a hit.

At 10th level, your companion finds new ways to help you in combat. Once per turn, after an attack you can choose for your companion to do one of the following if they are within 5ft of you or the enemy:
The attack's target takes 1d8 necrotic damage from the companion.
The attack's target must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your CE save DC or be moved by the shikigami up to 15 feet horizontally in a direction of your choice and knocked prone.
You are moved by the companion 5 feet horizontally in a direction of your choice, gaining half cover until the beginning of your next turn.
Beginning at 13th level, your shikigami grows stronger. Your companion gains the following benefits:
You can spread out 4 points among its ability scores (max of 20).
Its strike attacks deal 1d6 extra necrotic damage(total of 2d6).
You can either choose for your shikigami to become large, or gain the ability to become any weapon, dealing an additional 2d6 necrotic damage.

At 17th level, your character is rescued at the last moment by your shikigami. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to give yourself resistance to that damage. You are moved by your companion and you are moved to an unoccupied space that you can see within your companion’s movement speed, where you reappear with the shikigami.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a long rest.
At 20th level, your companion no longer needs to be commanded, having perfect synchronicity. Your companion no longer takes any action to command, and you can share senses with it.

As an action for 5 Cursed Energy, you cover the area around you within a 2165-foot radius with a black dome for 10 minutes. Upon activation, a dark, almost liquid-like matter drips down from the sky to form the outer barrier wall in the shape of a half-sphere. The curtain changes the sky into night, provoking cursed spirits out of hiding. For each 1 extra Cursed Energy you spend, you add +1 minute to the curtain's duration. Those without cursed energy, or magic cannot see anything inside the barrier, merely seeing as if nothing but the vegetation was there. Creatures who can see into the ethereal plane or have levels in a sorcerer class can see the black half-sphere.
Your curtain has a number of hit points equal to your
Cursed Energy modifier times your level. At 7th level, your curtains have health equal to your cursed energy modifier times 25, and at 13th level, it is 50 times your cursed energy modifier.

At 2nd level, you have learned how to create basic barriers to protect areas or trap opponents and protect allies. As an action for up to your Cursed Energy modifier in cursed energy, you make a dome starting from yourself with a 5-foot radius and a 10-foot height. For each cursed energy spent, the barrier can increase its width by 10 feet and its height by 10 feet. This barrier has 10 hit points per cursed energy spent and is immune to Poison and Psychic damage. This barrier lasts a number of minutes equal to your Cursed Energy modifier. At 9th level, your barriers have health equal to 20 times the cursed energy spent, and at 15th level it is resistant to damage from the outside.

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 14th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. You can also ignore this increase to instead gain a Feat.

Starting at 5th level, you have been born with a great aptitude for healing others, despite never really studying medicine. You will gain the Reverse Cursed Technique feature. Your reverse cursed technique is stronger than normal, letting you use 20 hit points from your RCT pool per cursed energy spent instead of 10.

In addition, you gain proficiency in the Medicine skill. If you are already proficient, you gain expertise instead. If you already have expertise you gain advantage. Whenever you make a medicine check to stabilize someone and succeed, the creature regains 1 hit point.
When you reach 10th level, you have reached new heights with this new type of energy, becoming a high-level sorcerer. You will gain the following benefits:
You can cause a creature you touch to gain the benefits of reverse cursed technique instead of you.
You can use your reverse cursed technique once as a free action on your turn.
Your reverse cursed technique healing pool is multiplied by your Cursed Energy modifier again.
You now regain 30 HP per CE with RCT instead of 20.

In addition, whenever you deal damage to a Monstrosity, Undead, or Cursed Spirit with an unarmed strike or natural weapon, you can spend cursed energy to remove hit points from your healing pool to add radiant damage.
Beginning at 17th level, you have mastered this new type of energy, becoming a high-level sorcerer. You will gain the following benefits:
You can use your reverse cursed technique twice as a free action on your turn.
Your reverse cursed technique healing pool is doubled.
You now regain 35 hit points per cursed energy instead of 30.

In addition, whenever you deal damage to a Monstrosity, Undead, or Cursed Spirit with an unarmed strike or natural weapon, you can spend cursed energy to remove hit points from your healing pool to add radiant damage, the creature takes this damage as vulnerable.
At 20th level, you can maintain your curtains and barriers (not Domains) until the barriers are destroyed.

Starting at 1st level, you were born with an Innate Technique. Innate Techniques are unique abilities congenitally engraved into the user's body, specifically in the right prefrontal cortex of the brain. Most jujutsu sorcerers are born with an innate technique that manifests around the age of five or six, which continually carves its formula into the user over time. You must choose one Innate Technique, all detailed under Innate Techniques. Your choice grants you features at 1st, and again at 3rd, 6th, 11th, and 18th level

At 1st level, your life of scrapping and battling with beasts, humans, or other tough creatures has given you mastery of Combat styles that use unarmed strikes and Warrior weapons, which are melee weapons without the two-handed property, and improvised weapons. You can not use the finesse property of a weapon while using it as a Warrior weapon.
You can roll a d6 in place of the normal damage of your unarmed strike or Warrior weapon. This die changes as you gain Warrior levels, as shown in the scrapper column on the Warrior table.

When you use the Attack action with an unarmed strike or a Warrior weapon on your turn, you can make one unarmed strike or grapple as a bonus action. For example, if you take the Attack action and Attack with a Club, you can also make an Unarmed Strike or grapple as a Bonus Action, assuming you haven’t already taken a Bonus Action this turn.
While you are not wearing any armor and not using a shield, your Armor Class equals 10 + your Dexterity modifier + your Constitution

At 2nd level, even after being damaged you still stand and fight as if nothing happened. On your turn, you can use a bonus action to regain hit points equal to 1d10 + your warrior level. You gain a second use at 10th level.
Once you use this feature, you must finish a short or long rest before you can use it again.

When you reach 4th level, and again at 8th, 12th, 16th, and 19th level, you can increase one ability score of your choice by 2, or you can increase two ability scores of your choice by 1. You can also ignore this increase to instead gain a Feat.
Once you get to 5th level, you can attack twice, instead of
once, whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.
The number of attacks increases to three when you reach 11th level in this class, to four when you reach 17th level in this class, and to five when you reach 20th level.
Starting at 7th level, your awareness and preparation reached a new and constant state. This gives you advantage on initiative checks.
Beginning at 9th level, you can reroll a saving throw that you fail. If you do so, you must use the new roll, and you can't use this feature again until you finish a long rest.
You can use this feature twice between long rests starting at 13th level.
Once you reach 14th level, your mastery of Cursed Energy grants you proficiency in all saving throws.
At 15th level, you hold great mastery over your attacks. When you miss an attack you can reroll the attack roll
You can create devastating fields of antigravity.

Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.

Starting at 1st level, you have learned how to use your technique to manipulate gravity, allowing you to make a small gravitational field around yourself. As an action for 3 cursed energy, you can reverse gravity in a 10 foot-radius 30 foot-high cylinder centered on you for all creatures but yourself until the beginning of your next turn.

All creatures and objects that aren’t anchored to the ground in the area fall upward. A creature can make a Dexterity saving throw to grab onto a fixed object it can reach, thus avoiding the fall. If a solid object (such as a ceiling) is encountered in this fall, falling objects and creatures strike it and take the remaining height as fall damage. If an object or creature reaches the top of the area without striking anything, it remains there, oscillating slightly, for the
duration. At the end of the duration, affected objects and creatures fall back down, taking fall damage.

The height of the cylinder increases to 50 feet at 3rd level, 100 feet at 11th level and 200 feet at 18th level. Fall damage from this technique ignores any type of fall damage reduction or immunity. Fall damage die becomes d8 at 3rd level and d10 at 6th level.
At 3rd level, you gained the following benefits through practicing your technique.
As a reaction for 1 CE to falling, you and creatures equal to your proficiency bonus within 120 feet have their rate of descent slowed to 60 feet per round and take no fall damage when you land.

must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, they make any attacks at disadvantage and cannot maintain concentration while within your field.

If you are taking the Dodge action, you can use this reaction on another creature within 5 feet.

As an action for 8 cursed energy, you can launch up to 3 giant centipedes at targets within 120 feet, making a ranged cursed energy attack roll for each. On a hit, they deal 8d10 necrotic damage and the target must make a Strength saving throw. On a failure, the target is pushed or pulled 30ft closer or further (your choice) and falls prone.

Additionally, you can now have two cursed centipedes summoned at a time. While you have two cursed centipedes acting as your shroud, you can make 2 melee attacks as a bonus action and instead add 3 + your proficiency bonus to your AC.
At 18th level, you have mastered your technique allowing you to open your domain. Within your domain, your cursed centipedes’s attacks are

guaranteed hits. At initiative 20, all creatures are restrained by cursed centipedes and can make a Strength (Athletics) check at the beginning of their turns to escape. The centipedes restraining a creature assists all attacks against the target, causing such attacks to deal an additional 2d10 damage. The cursed centipedes disappear once the domain ends or the creature is no longer grappled.
Your technique allows you to create perfect clones of yourself.

Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.

Starting at 1st level, you can spend 3 CE as an action to create a clone within 5 feet of yourself for 8 hours. They are completely indistinguishable from you in every way. A clone has 1/4 of your hit point maximum (rounded up) as well as your AC and access to all your class features and cursed techniques, but not innate technique features. Any cursed energy or features used is treated as if you spent it. Your Clones act on your turn, but can only make one attack on their turn even if you have Extra Attack or bonus action attacks. You can replace any of your attacks on your turn with an attack from the Clone’s space. Your Clones do not have any of your items.
You can have a number of clones equal to your proficiency bonus at once and when a clone dies, the number of clones you can have is reduced by 1 for 1 minute.

At 3rd level, you can now create multiple clones as an action by spending 3 CE for each clone. When you make a melee attack against a creature while a Clone is within 5 feet of the target, you gain advantage on the attack roll.

At 6th level you have become more skillful and efficient with the creation of your clones. Your Clones now have 1/2 of your total hit points. When one of your Clones is reduced to 0 hit points, you regain 1 cursed energy.

At 11th level, you have mastered the ability to choose which of your Clones is your actual body. Your Clones have hit points equal to yours and you can swap bodies with one of your clones as a bonus action for 1 CE, trading hit points and causing that Clone to become your new body. When you are reduced to 0 hit points or killed outright while you have a Clone active, you can instead transfer yourself into one of your clones, gaining the Clone’s current hit points.
Your Clones can now create one Clone by spending your Cursed Energy with each Clone counting against your limit.

Finally at 18th level you have perfected your technique, allowing you to expand your domain. You can now create one Clone as a bonus action without spending cursed energy once per turn (Your Clones do not gain this benefit). Within your domain, you can have an unlimited number of Clones. Your Clone’s attacks are guaranteed hits within your domain.
At initiative 20, an additional clone appears. All Clones created with your domain disappear when the domain ends.

Each cube has an AC equal to your cursed energy DC and hit points equal to 5 times your CE modifier.

You can move a creature using these cubes. When creating the cubes in a creature’s area, you can attempt to move the target to a space within 5 feet. The creature must make a Dexterity saving throw, being pushed on a failure. As a bonus action, you can spend CE up to your proficiency bonus to protect yourself with earth. For 1 minute, you gain a bonus to your AC equal to the cursed energy spent.

As an action, you can spend 3 cursed energy to strike the ground. Creatures in a 20-foot radius around yourself must make a Dexterity saving throw. equal to your cursed energy DC and a number of hit points equal to 10 times your CE modifier.

You can spend 1 CE as a bonus action to move connected panels within 60 feet of you up to 30 feet in a direction of your choice that is in contact with the ground. If this movement would move a creature, they must make a Dexterity saving throw or be pushed by the wall.

On a success, they are not restrained and take half damage.

You can also choose to keep the hands active by spending 1 CE at the start of your turns. arms, they have AC 18 and HP equal to your maximum hit points and you must maintain concentration.

At 1st level, you can strike a pose and move so quickly it seems as if time has stopped. As a bonus action for 1 cursed energy you can stop time until the end of your turn. During stopped time, you cannot use cursed energy, and are affected by the following:
You have advantage on all attack rolls against creatures in stopped time.
Ranged attacks you make become affected by stopped time and are suspended in mid-air, but finish when time resumes.
Other creatures in stopped time automatically fail Strength and Dexterity saves and cannot use reactions. (A creature can use
their reaction against a ranged attack you have made once time has resumed.)

At 3rd level, you can instead spend up to twice your proficiency bonus in cursed energy as a Full Turn Action (Action + Bonus Action + Movement) to strike a majestic pose and immediately take one turn per three CE spent in stopped time. Doing so places extreme stress on your body. Once time resumes your movement speed is reduced to 0 until the end of your next turn.
When you stop time, your speed increases by 10 ft until time resumes. This increases by 5 ft at 6th, 11th, and 18th level.

At 6th level, you have begun to master your technique. You have learned to use your technique for longer. As an action for 4 cursed energy instead of stopping time you can empower yourself for longer,
gaining the following benefits for 1 minute:
You gain a +3 bonus to AC.
You have advantage on Dexterity saving throws.
You gain an additional action on each of its turns. That action can be used only to take the Attack (one weapon attack only), Dash, Disengage, Hide, or Use an Object action.
You cannot stop time until this feature ends.

At 11th level, you have gained the limited ability to reverse time. As a Full Turn Action (Action + Bonus Action + Movement) for 8 cursed energy you can strike a supreme pose and rewind time by 6 seconds, taking all creatures and objects within 100 ft back in time 1 round to the start of your previous turn.

Any damage taken or cursed energy spent (other than this technique) during that round is undone and all creatures are taken back to where they were 6 seconds ago as long as it is within the 100 ft radius of the rewind.
Finally at 18th level, you have created a domain imbued with your perfected technique. At initiative 20, you can stop time and
immediately take one turn as your domain empowers you. Whenever you stop time in your domain using your technique, you stop time for an additional turn.
Your technique allows you to form your hair into a variety of shapes.

Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.

Beginning at 1st level, you have learned to move your hair into different forms using cursed energy. When you take the Attack action, you can spend 1 CE to replace an attack by shaping your hair into a barbed stinger. Make a melee cursed energy attack against a creature within 10 ft of you. On a hit you deal 1d10 + your CE modifier piercing damage. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls with this attack at 3rd level. This increases to a +2 bonus at 6th level, +3 bonus at 11th level and +4 bonus at 18th level.

At 3rd level, you have learned to form your hair into drill bits and shoot them off as projectiles. When you take the Attack action, you can spend 1 cursed energy to replace an attack with a ranged cursed energy attack roll with a range of 30ft. This attack deals 1d6 + your CE modifier piercing damage. The range of this technique increases to

When attacking with a drill, you can spend an additional 2 cursed energy to make the drill explode in a 5 ft radius upon the point of impact causing creatures in range to make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they take an additional 3d6 fire damage. On a success, they take half as much damage. The fire damage increases to 5d6 at 6th level, 8d6 at 11th level and 10d6 at 18th level.

At 6th level you have learned to make more complex constructs from your hair. As an action for 3 CE, you form your hair into either a Jet or Helicopter for 1 minute and can spend 1 CE to keep the form active for 1 minute:

. You gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed and can take the Dash action as a bonus action. When you take the attack action, you can spend 2 cursed energy to replace one attack by extending your blades and attempting to slash an enemy. Make a melee cursed energy attack, on a hit you deal 6d8 + your CE modifier slashing damage. This damage increases to 8d8 at 11th level, and 10d8 at 18th level.
A creature that hits you with an Opportunity attack takes slashing damage equal to your CE modifier. This becomes twice your CE modifier at 11th level.
. You gain a flying speed equal to your walking speed. When you take the dash action while flying, you not only do not provoke

opportunity attacks, but can also choose to move in a straight line and crash through creatures. All creatures in your path must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, they take Xd8 bludgeoning damage and are pushed back 30 ft away from you and knocked prone. If they impact a solid surface, they take 1d4 bludgeoning for every 10 ft you traveled in a straight line before crashing into them. On a successful save they take half as much damage and are not pushed or knocked prone. (X = CE modifier)
At 11th level, taking the Dash action while flying you instead move up to twice your flying speed. This increases to three times your flying speed at 18th level.

At 11th level, your hair has become almost indestructible, allowing you to grow it to longer lengths and activate your techniques more freely. The melee reach of your techniques increases by 5 ft and your hair counts as a Grade 1 Cursed Tool. At 18th level, your hair counts as a Special Grade Cursed Tool.

Once per turn you can spend 2 additional CE to activate one of your technique features requiring an attack roll as a bonus action. An attack roll made using this special free action is made at advantage. Alternatively, once per turn you can spend 4 CE to activate one of your technique features requiring a saving throw as a bonus action. A saving throw forced by this special free action is made at disadvantage.

Finally at 18th level you have learned to expand your domain. Creatures other than you take 2d10 slashing damage for every 5 ft they move within your domain as infinitesimally small and sharp hairs cut into them with their every movement. Your domain counts as difficult terrain for creatures other than you.
A simple yet effective technique, powered by the heart.

Starting at 1st level, you create a pair of translucent hands as a bonus action for 1 Cursed Energy. These hands stay within 15 ft of you and each count as medium constructs. You can replace any attacks you make on your turn with an attack from your

. These hands deal your unarmed damage, and have advantage on grappling and shoving. The hands have an AC equal to your Cursed Energy save DC, HP equal to twice your cursed energy score and you take 1/10th of damage they take. This increases to three times your cursed energy score at 6th level and four times at 11th level.
At 3rd level, your love hands improve. Your hands gain the following benefits:
Your hands AC increase by your proficiency bonus
Your hands gain a damage bonus equal to your CE modifier
The range of your hands increases to a total of 30 feet
You can use cursed feats and abilities using your hands
to guard a creature within 5 ft of both hands, granting them three quarters cover. Alternatively, you can have each hand guard a different target to grant them half cover.

Starting at 11th level, on a hit you can spend 5 Cursed Energy to force a creature you hit with a melee attack to become Charmed. A creature charmed in this way can only target you with attacks and harmful effects for 1 minute and must make a Wisdom save at the start of their turn to end the condition.

At 18th level, you have learned the true meaning of love. At initiative 20 all creatures in the Domain are restrained and charmed until the end of their next turn. Additionally, your Love Hands automatically hit all attack rolls and creatures automatically fail grapple and shove checks as well as saving throws made by the hands.
Your technique is beautiful in its simplicity, and the ability to make and control ice.

Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.

Beginning at 1st level, your innate technique has allowed you to mess with the temperature around you, creating extreme levels of cold. As an action for 1 cursed energy, you can force creatures in a 10ft cone to make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they take 1d10 cold damage and are restrained as ice covers part of their bodies. On a success, they take half as much damage and are not restrained.
The creature can make a Strength saving throw at the beginning of its turns to break the ice and end the restrained condition.
All ice created by your technique will last until you end it as a free action, a creature breaks it, or you are poisoned, incapacitated, or unconscious.
At 3rd level, the damage of this feature increases to 2d10, to 3d10 at 6th, to 4d10 at 10th, to 5d10 at 14th, and to 6d10 cold damage at 20th level.

At 3rd level, being stuck on your ice feels like staying in a cold mountain while you wait for death. A creature inside your ice is under one level of Exhaustion. Any creatures within 5ft of your ice that don't have resistance or immunity to cold damage have their movement speed halved.

When you reach 6th level, you have learned how to unleash thick layers of ice through the mist. As an action for 4 cursed energy, you can send a cloud of freezing mist to a spot within 60 feet of you. Every creature in a 30-foot radius sphere in that spot must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they take 6d8 cold damage and are restrained by an ice layer. On a success, they take half as much damage and are not restrained.
The creature can make a Strength saving throw at the beginning of its turns to break the ice and end the restrained condition.

Once you reach 11th level, you learn a great execution method that makes sure your enemies won't escape. As an action for 8 cursed energy, you fall prone until the beginning of your next turn to create ice on the ground. You telepathically manipulate the ice created, launching one for every creature within 30 ft of you of your choice. Make a cursed energy attack roll, on a hit they take 1d10 cold damage and become restrained.
The creature can make a Strength saving throw at the beginning of its turns to break the ice and end the

Hitting or missing, giant spikes of ice will fall from the sky on top of the targeted creatures, forcing them to make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they take 6d8 cold damage and 6d8 piercing damage. On a success, they take half as much damage.

If you achieve 18th level, you hone your technique to a fine edge, allowing you to use your Domain Expansion. While inside it, every creature except you takes 10d8 cold damage and is restrained at the end of their turn. A creature can make a Strength (Athletics) check at the beginning of their turn to break out.
The soul is an interesting thing and your technique manipulates it.

Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.

Starting at 1st level, your touch can alter a creature's very own being, their soul. Whenever you hit a creature with a natural weapon, unarmed strike, or touch them, you can deal an additional 1d6 Necrotic damage.

In addition, as an action for 1 Cursed Energy, you can force a creature within your reach to make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, they will take 1d10 Necrotic Damage, which increases to 2d10 at 3rd level, 3d10 at 6th level, 4d10 at 11th level, and 5d10 at 18th level. On a success, the creature takes half as much damage. This damage reduces a creature’s hit point maximum until they finish a long rest.
If Necrotic damage from any features of Idle Transfiguration reduces a creature's total hit points to 0, the creature will become one of your Transfigured Creatures. This does not work on Constructs.

You can have a number of transfigured creatures equal to your level x your Cursed Energy modifier. Transfigured creatures will follow your orders, act at the end of your turn and their creature type is undead. On a short or long rest, you can modify a transfigured creature’s size from tiny to huge.
The creature’s mental scores will be decreased to 4. You can redistribute the points removed from their mental stats into their physical scores, even beyond 20.
Transformed creatures lose all supernatural abilities like cursed technique as well as proficiencies, and their AC is 10 + Dexterity modifier. They
can only use natural weapons or unarmed attacks. They roll a d6 in place of the normal damage of their unarmed strike.

You can command with simple orders such as to attack a creature as a bonus action. Complex orders like area control are an action. You can store transfigured creatures, extracting any number as an action.
Beginning at 3rd level, you can safely alter yourself or an ally.
You can use your alteration on willing creatures, to alter them as you see fit. You alter a willing creature during a short or long rest, granting them one or more of the following benefits:
The creature gains advantage in perception checks involving smell.
The creature gains advantage in perception checks involving hearing.
The creature gains advantage in perception checks involving seeing.
The creature gains darkvision up to 60 feet, if the creature already has darkvision it will extend its range by 30 feet.
The creature gains resistance to either: bludgeoning, slashing, or piercing.
The creature gains a swimming speed equal to its walking speed and can breathe underwater.
You can grant a number of different alterations to the same creature equal to your proficiency.
You have learned how to shape your own form in many different ways. As a bonus action, you can gain new body parts. You
can choose one of the following:
Your unarmed strikes deal slashing and count as light, finesse, martial melee weapons
Your unarmed strikes deal piercing damage, and increases damage by your Proficiency
Increase movement by 10 feet and Bonus Action dash.
As a reaction to a melee attack within 5 feet, you can deal Piercing damage equal to 4x your Proficiency.
You gain a 60 ft fly speed. While at least 15 feet away, you gain a +2 bonus to AC
No Spike Hands, Sword Hands, Arm Shield, or Long Arms
At 6th level, you gain the following

. For 2 CE, you increase or decrease your size by 1 category for 1 min (does not stack). While enlarged you have advantage on Strength checks and Strength saving throws and your unarmed strikes deal 1d4 extra damage. While reduced you have advantage on Dexterity checks and saves and a +1 to AC. You can revert as a bonus action.

At 6th level, you have learned how to create a near perfect clone of yourself. As an action for 6 Cursed Energy, you create a copy of yourself, giving it half of your current and max Hit Points and Cursed Energy. It is identical to you, controlled by you, acts at the end of your turn, and you can view through its senses. Your clone cannot use your Innate Technique features except Self-Alteration. You can't make another clone until it dies or you touch it and rejoin, granting you back the rest of your max HP and Cursed Energy.
Starting at 11th level, you can use
as a free action on your turn. As an action for 5 Cursed Energy you can spend 2 or more Transfigured Creatures, fusing together for one of the following:

You create a barrage of Transfigured creatures being launched at high speeds. You make a ranged Cursed Energy attack with a range of 60/120 feet that deals 4d8 necrotic damage on a hit. For every additional Transfigured Creature, you deal another 1d8 necrotic damage and can split the damage die between different targets to make multiple attacks.
You create a Polymorphic Soul Isomer for 1 minute. When using this technique, you can add another Transfigured Creature to the
fusion. Each transfigured creature counts as one soul.
Domain Expansion: Self Embodiment of Perfection

Finally, at 18th level, you have studied your powers and have finally learned your most powerful technique. You create a large dimension filled with your body parts, making escaping death impossible. At initiative 20 creatures within your domain suffer twice your
Your technique lets you curse people and make them see illusions.

At 1st level, your technique allows you to curse creatures and make them see other people's faces in a distorted way. You are also able to track those you have cursed. As an action for 2 cursed energy, you can curse a creature within 60 feet. The target must make a Charisma saving throw. On a failure, the next person they see has a distorted face. Upon seeing this distortion for the first time, the creature must make an Intelligence saving throw. On a failure, the creature is confused and has disadvantage on attack rolls and Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma checks until the end of their next turn. A sorcerer can repeat the Charisma save at the end of their turns to end the curse.

When a creature fails their Charisma saving throw, you gain the ability to track them up to 400 feet away. While a creature is cursed, you know its general location. The cursed creature keeps seeing the distorted face until they succeed the save or leave your tracking range.

At 6th level, you can target a number of creatures up to your Cursed Energy modifier as an action, spending 2 CE for each. Additionally, a creature that fails its save also has disadvantage on Intelligence, Wisdom, and Charisma saves and loses concentration on any technique or feature it was concentrating on.
At 3rd level, you’ve learned how to distort your own body to confuse your opponents. You learn the 3 following distortion techniques:

. As part of making a melee attack, you can spend 3 cursed energy to create a duplicate of your weapon. Make a melee cursed attack roll at disadvantage, afterwards you make your normal attack against the same target. If the phase attack misses the actual attack will deal double the damage dice on a hit and if the phase attack hits the main attack will instead be made at advantage.

. As an action for 3 cursed energy, your body becomes blurred, shifting and wavering to all who can see you. For a number of rounds equal to your Cursed Energy modifier, a creature that can see you has disadvantage on attack rolls against you. An attacker is immune to this effect if it doesn't rely on sight like blindsight or can see through illusions like with true sight.

. For 3 cursed energy, you make yourself (including your clothing, armor, weapons, and other belongings) look different for a number of hours equal to your Cursed Energy modifier. The changes of this feature fail to hold up to physical inspection. For example, if you use this technique to add a hat to your outfit, objects pass through the hat, and anyone who touches it would feel nothing or would feel your head and hair. If you use this spell to appear thinner than you are, the hand of someone who reaches out to touch you would bump into you while it was seemingly still in midair. To discern that you are disguised, a creature can use its action to inspect your appearance and must succeed on an Intelligence
(Investigation) check against your cursed energy save DC.

At 6th level, you have now learned a new way to distort the surroundings of those you have cursed. As an action, you may choose an object within the range of your cursed illusion that you can see to distort its appearance, this can include changing its opacity, luster, visible texture, or its seen value. A creature can attempt to discern the illusion by rolling an investigation check against your cursed energy save DC. You can spend an additional 3 CE to make the object invisible. If a creature runs into a medium or larger invisible object, they take 1d6 bludgeoning and lose their reaction.
The cost of the technique depends on the size of the targeted object:

At 11th level, you have decided that affecting the area around people can lead to strategic victory. As an action for 10 cursed energy, you can manipulate the surrounding terrain around you in a 150 ft radius in the following ways:
. You make the terrain appear difficult to traverse, when a creature attempts to walk in this area they must spend twice as much movement per 5 ft of travel.
. As an action, you make a false structure or wall within range. A creature is convinced that the structure is real, meaning that they cannot target you with features that require line of sight.

A creature can attempt to see through the illusion by rolling an Investigation or Perception check (using their Cursed Energy score if they are a Sorcerer) against your Cursed Energy save DC. A creature automatically succeeds if they have an ability like true sight.

At 18th level, you have mastered your technique allowing you to open your domain. At initiative 20, you can force all creatures to fall under an illusion of your choice. Additionally, you can use your reaction to trick a creature that attacks you to target a random creature within range. They must roll a dice to see who is targeted with the dice depending on the number of creatures within range. On a 1, you are still targeted. On a higher roll, a different creature is targeted. If there are no other creatures in range, roll a d2. On a 2, the attack targets a random direction, missing you completely.
You invert damage taken based on a specific threshold.

Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.

Starting at 1st level, you gain the ability to invert the damage you take. As a bonus action, you can spend 2 cursed energy to activate Inverse for 1 minute. While Inverse is active, when you take damage, it is modified based on a damage limit and threshold. The damage limit equals your proficiency bonus times your Cursed Energy score, and the threshold is equal to your proficiency bonus times your Cursed Energy modifier.

When you take damage that exceeds your threshold, you subtract the threshold from the damage and take the remaining difference as damage. However, when the damage is below your threshold, you subtract the threshold from the damage and take the resulting number as damage instead. For example, if your set limit is 100 and you take 90 damage, you would subtract the damage from your limit if it exceeds the threshold (e.g., 90 - 20 = 70), and take the remaining 70 damage. Conversely, if the damage is below the threshold (e.g., 10 damage), you subtract that amount from your set limit (100 - 10 = 90), and take 90 damage instead. If the calculation results in a negative number, the damage remains unchanged.
You can extend the duration of Inverse by spending 1 cursed energy to maintain the effect for an additional minute.

At 3rd level, you’ve learned to further manipulate the damage you take based on its intensity. If you take damage that is below your threshold, you are considered vulnerable to the damage dealt. However, if the damage exceeds your threshold, you gain resistance to the damage, even if it would normally bypass resistances or immunities.

For example, if your threshold is 15 and you take 10 damage, you treat that as vulnerability. But if you take 18 damage, you instead halve it due to your resistance, even if that type of damage would normally ignore resistances.

At 6th level, you’ve become adept at manipulating damage based on its intensity, even when making saving throws. When you are forced to make a saving throw against an effect that deals damage, the difficulty of the save depends on whether the damage is above or below your threshold.

If the damage is above your threshold, you have advantage on the saving throw, regardless of the damage type. If the damage is below your threshold, you have disadvantage on the saving throw, as weaker attacks become more dangerous to you.

For example, if your threshold is 15 and you would take 18 damage from a fireball, you gain advantage on the saving throw. However, if you take 10 damage from the same attack, you would roll with disadvantage instead.

At 11th level, staying with your technique active for long periods of time can become a disadvantage at times, so you have trained to have easier access to your technique. You can now use your technique as a reaction to damage and can deactivate your technique as a reaction.

In addition, you now have additional reactions equal to half of your proficiency bonus(rounded up) that can be used only for the inverse technique. At 18th level, this becomes a number of reactions equal to your proficiency bonus.

At 18th level, you have mastered your technique allowing you to open your domain. Within your domain, you can activate Inverse as a free action an infinite number of times for no cost. At initiative 20, creatures of your choice have their senses inverted. Each creature rolls a d4 (1: taste, 2: smell, 3: touch, 4: sight) having a sense inverted and unable to be used. A creature can make a Cursed Energy check at the end of their turn to regain their lost sense.
A thought experiment proposing an intellect so vast it knows the position and momentum of every particle, allowing it to predict the future and recall the past.

Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.

Starting at 1st level, you have extreme control of your emotions with a logical mindset allowing you to use Intelligence as your Cursed Energy modifier. You can spend 1 CE as a bonus action to overclock your brain for 1 minute, gaining the following benefits:
You can spend 2 CE to take an action as a reaction.
You gain advantage on Intelligence checks.
You add your Intelligence modifier to AC and Dexterity saves.
You gain the 2000 IQ Skill feat.
Starting at 3rd level, you can accelerate your brain to predict the future and past with frightful accuracy.
When you finish a long rest, roll two d20s and record the numbers rolled. You can spend 1 CE as a reaction to replace any attack roll,
saving throw, or ability check you make, or a saving throw you force another creature to make with one of these foretelling rolls. You must choose to do so before the roll.

Each foretelling roll can be used only once. When you finish a long rest, you lose any unused foretelling rolls. When you complete a short rest, you can spend 1 CE to gain another foretelling roll. You can only have one foretelling roll from a short rest at a time.

At 6th level, you have learned to overload the minds of others instead of your own. As an action for 4 cursed energy you can touch a creature and force them to make an Intelligence saving throw. On a failure they take 5d10 psychic damage and are stunned until the end of their next turn, on a success they take half as much damage and aren’t stunned.

At 11th level, you have learned to push the effects of your technique to their maximum limit. As an action, you can spend 8 cursed energy to enter a state of elevated intellect and foresight for 1 hour. All rolls you make are at advantage and all rolls against you are at disadvantage as you are able to see through the truth of the world in its entirety. As a reaction, you can add your Intelligence modifier to an attack roll, skill check or saving throw made by you or a creature within 15 ft of you.

At 18th level you have mastered your technique allowing you to expand your domain. At initiative 20, all creatures of your choice within your domain gain a cumulative -2 penalty to all rolls against you as you begin to see the state of every atom.
You know the hit points, cursed energy, effects, conditions, resistances, immunities, and vulnerabilities of all creatures within the domain.
Invisible creatures are always visible to you.
Creatures cannot gain advantage against you from being unseen or hidden.
A technique whose power is only matched by its complexity,

On a 4 or higher, any attacks or spells made against you automatically fail to touch or

You can spend 1 Cursed Energy to automatically roll a 6 on an Infinity roll. This feature does not work against poison or attacks that you cannot see until 6th level.

This pulls targets within a radius of 5 feet for each CE spent, forcing a Strength saving throw. On a failure, they take 2d8 + 1d8 for each CE in force damage and are dragged into the blue and grappled. At 11th level, on a failure of 5 or more they take maximum damage and are restrained. When you spend at least 5 CE on

form to make it last for up to a minute while concentrating. As bonus action, you can move the sphere 30 ft in any direction. All creatures currently stuck in the sphere are also moved and a creature that starts their turn in range must make the saving throw. You

At 6th level, your control over blue and space has increased. As an action, you can teleport yourself or another willing creature you touch 10 ft per Cursed Energy used.

You can teleport an additional creature by doubling the cursed energy cost. Additionally, with the use of a binding vow, you can instead teleport a creature to a 5 ft circle you have prepared. You can teleport a willing creature you touch to one of these circles as an action for 5 cursed energy. You can only have one circle per binding vow.
At 11th level, you have learned to push infinity to an aggressive mode through offensive training. As an action, you can spend CE up to your Cursed Energy modifier to amplify

, a creature within 5 ft makes this save at disadvantage.

, you can spend CE up to your modifier at the start of your turn to maintain the technique, forcing the creature to repeat the save.
