Love Rendezvous is a technique based on the Southern Cross. It marks creatures or objects with cursed energy and makes the lowest star have to pass through the other ones before they can move.

Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.

Starting at 1st level, you have a very complex technique, and you have learned the basics of how to use it. As a free action when you touch a creature or object(this can be done with yourself) with cursed energy or as part of hitting an unarmed strike, you can spend 1 cursed energy to mark the target's cursed energy with a star of your choice. Only one star can be placed in one creature's cursed energy at a time, however the same star can be applied to different people's cursed energy at a time. You can mark a number of creatures with the same star up to your Cursed Energy modifier. If you mark a creature, everything that has their cursed energy will be marked as well, like Shikigami, cursed tools etc.
The following stars are available to mark:
When you mark a creature, a sparking light will appear above their head. They can also find the star's name marked on their body with a Wisdom (Perception) check.

Anyone appointed with a star must follow a sequential order if they want to attempt approaching another star. When they make their movement, they must move directly towards the next star in order and touch them, which allows them to move on to the next star in order. Failing to do this will make them restrained until the beginning of their next turn and every single creature or object marked with the same star will be attracted to the point with the highest cursed energy, being all rapidly thrown at that point. The highest cursed energy point will take 1 dice of bludgeoning damage per 5ft the other stars have travelled and their size, while the objects and creatures that crashed into it will take half as much damage. See the following chart for measure of damage:
The order of the stars is as follows: ★Imai → ★Acrux → ★Mimosa → ★Ginan → ★Gacrux

If there is no possible path for a target to follow the order, the target isn’t affected by the technique until such a possible path is created. The target is immediately affected again once such a path exists. For example, if Gacrux is placed in front of Ginan for a creature marked with Acrux, then the technique no longer functions for that creature, as there is no way to touch Ginan without approaching Gacrux. Once the creature passes Gacrux, thus opening a path for them to get to Ginan, the technique functions for them once more, and they must touch Ginan before approaching Gacrux.
The stars last for 10 minutes or until you remove one or more of them.

Creatures won't know they're being affected by the technique until they suffer the consequences from not following the order. After that, they can make a Perception check to find the star. After they discover the star, they can make a Wisdom (Insight) check at disadvantage against your cursed energy DC to try to understand your technique. Unless they have the Cursed Energy Perception feat or are familiar with the southern star constellation, which allows them to ignore

At 3rd level, you learned how to mark creatures in a quicker and more effective manner. You can now mark creatures with stars as a reaction. Also, you gain a number of additional reactions equal to your Cursed Energy modifier that can only be used to mark other creatures.

At 6th level, your technique's attraction has grown stronger. The damage of creatures colliding now ignores resistance to bludgeoning damage. This becomes force damage at 11th level and ignores resistance to force damage at 18th level.
At 11th level, you became better with your technique, now being able to have more stars. The amount of stars you can put of the same type is increased to twice your Cursed Energy modifier.

At 18th level, you have learned to expand your domain. At initiative 20, you can mark any creatures within your domain with any of your available stars. As an action, you can cause a creature marked with one of your stars to move up to 30 ft towards another marked target, taking collision damage if they impact and counting as part of your guaranteed hit. Any marks created by your domain disappear when your

Starting at 1st level, your technique brings you strength when you witness good fortune. When you witness this, you gain a Miracle. You can have up to six Miracles at once, which are stored as marks somewhere on your body. You gain 2 Miracles for every miracle you witness at 11th level and 3 Miracles at 18th level.
When you or an ally you can see rolls the maximum amount on a roll, you gain a Miracle.
Equal Numbers are supposed to be lucky, right?
When you or an ally you can see rolls two equal numbers one after the other, you gain a Miracle.
Finding free stuff is always cool!
When you or an ally you can see find an item worth $1,000 or more, you gain a Miracle.
Overcoming hardship is something rare in this harsh world, so every chance we get is a miracle.
When you or a creature you can see succeeds on a roll they had disadvantage on, you gain a Miracle.

Once per round when you take damage, you can spend a Miracle to reduce the incoming damage by Xd4 equal to your CE modifier. You add your proficiency bonus to the rolled amount and reduce the damage by that much. You can also do this as a reaction for a Miracle and 1 CE.
When used this way, the d4 increases to a d6 and you add your proficiency bonus twice.

At 3rd level, you can self-consciously alter fate. As a reaction to failing a roll you can spend 1 Miracle and 1 CE to add a d6 to the roll, potentially turning it into a success. This increases to a d8 at 6th level and a d10 at 11th level.

At 6th level, you have learned that out of difficulties, miracles grow. Your technique lets you fend off death by some miracle. When you are hit by an attack or fail a saving throw that would reduce you to 0 hit points or kill you outright, you can spend 2 Miracles and 2 CE to instead succeed the save or survive the attack and take no damage or additional effects. Completely escaping harm by seemingly dumb luck.
While you have at least 1 Miracle, you make death saving throws at advantage.
At 11th level, you can use this feature against an attack or effect that would reduce you to 1/2 or below your hit point maximum.
At 11th level you realize there is no bad future for you, only a path to fortune paved with miracles! If you roll 20 or higher using
, it is considered a critical success as if you had rolled a natural 20 (cannot roll for Black Flash or gain Miracle).
Domain Expansion: Luck of the Draw

Finally at 18th level you have mastered your technique allowing you to expand your domain. Your domain costs 2d20 CE to expand and lasts 1d4 minutes. If you lack the Cursed Energy, you must reattempt on your next turn and reroll the 2d20. If you expand your domain as a reaction to another Domain Expansion, you can choose to spend 20 CE or to roll 2d20.

At initiative 20, you gain 3 Miracles and have no limit on your max amount of Miracles. Within your domain, you can spend a Miracle on yourself or another creature when they make an attack or use a technique to imbue it with your guaranteed hit.
You can launch a barrage of giant fists against your opponents.

Beginning at 1st level, you learn the projection technique, which gives you the possibility to divide 1 second into 24 frames which allows you to move faster. As a bonus action for 1 Cursed Energy, your walking speed increases by 10 feet and you will gain an additional attack on your Attack Action. However, this cursed technique is not perfect as you cannot change your movement course once you start, so when your turn ends you pick the spot you want to move to, due to your speed it will be impossible to change course. If you do not end your turn in that space, your speed becomes 0 until the end of your next turn. You must spend 1 Cursed Energy at the beginning of your turns to keep this cursed technique active.
When you get to 3rd level, for every consecutive turn with
active your movement speed increases by 10 feet. If you charge in a straight line building momentum you can deal an additional d6 for every 10 feet on your next melee attack.

Once you reach 6th level, you have learned how to affect creatures with the 24 FPS rule, making them become stuck in one frame of animation. While your cursed technique is active, when you hit an unarmed strike on a creature you can choose to deal no damage by spending 2 Cursed Energy, forcing the creature to make an Intelligence saving throw. On a failure they will be stuck in one frame of animation, making them stunned until the beginning of your next turn. The creature loses its stunned condition early if it is hit by an attack which will automatically count as a critical. This critical ignores damage resistance and treats damage immunity as resistance.
At 11th level, due to your advanced studies, you can now reach a higher speed level than any sorcerer ever could. While your cursed technique is active, you will gain the following benefits:
You gain +30 feet to your walking speed.
You gain +20 feet to your walking speed at the beginning of your turns.
You have advantage on Dexterity saving throws.
Your Dexterity score increases by +2 ignoring your maximum.

Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. Beginning at 1st level, you gain mastery over puppets. You gain proficiency in Tinkerer’s Tools, and over a long rest, you can create a puppet. As an action for 1 Cursed Energy, you can imbue a Puppet, this puppet can only have 2 Minor Traits. You can summon as many puppets as you want. Any Puppets can only take an action if you use your bonus action to command it. It cannot use its reaction unless you use your reaction to command it to. The puppet can use bonus actions on its own. You can speak, hear, and see through any of your Puppets. In case you have more than one puppet at once, you need to control them at the same time. Whenever you gain a puppet, use the following for its sheet:

Your Puppet's starting Strength, Constitution, and Dexterity scores are 15, 14, and 13 + bonus points to distribute between them equal to your Cursed Energy modifier. The Puppet's mental scores equal to your own.
Your Puppet is a Medium Construct.

Your Puppet has its hit dice based on what material they are made from, if the case is wood is a d4, stone is a d6, iron is a d8, and modern metal hit die is a d10. Your puppet has the same amount of hit die as you.
Your Puppet has a 30 feet walking speed.
You control your Puppet from afar, watching its every move and controlling it to dodge attacks. Your Puppet's AC is equal to 10 + its Dexterity modifier.
Your Puppet uses your proficiency bonus and is immune to the charmed and poisoned condition.
Your Puppet gains proficiency in Strength, Constitution, and Dexterity saving throws.
Your Puppet deals 1d6 + Strength modifier in bludgeoning with unarmed strikes.
Your Puppet's defenses were increased so that he could fare better against attacks. Its armor class is increased to 10 + its Dexterity modifier + your Cursed Energy modifier.
Your puppet gains proficiency in simple weapons and shields.
Your puppet is fast and cannot be caught so easily. Your puppet gains a +10 ft bonus to its walking speed.

Your puppet gains better natural weapons, changing its unarmed strikes to deal 1d8 piercing, slashing, or bludgeoning damage, based on the new weapons. Your puppet's unarmed strikes will now overcome resistance. Your puppet can use dexterity or strength for these attacks.
Your puppet is always sharp and is a perfect detection machine. He will gain 60 ft. of Darkvision and will gain advantage in perception checks against living things.
Your puppet's arms elongate, its agility heightens, or it grows tentacles, and your puppet's melee reach increases by 5 feet.
Your puppet gains proficiency in martial weapons.
Your puppet's shell is thicker, scalier, or harder than normal. Your Puppet will gain resistance against non-magical Bludgeoning, Slashing, or Piercing damage.

Your puppet has developed quick reaction skills, and can now defend itself from high-speed ranged projectiles. Using its reaction, your puppet can reduce an incoming projectile damage by 1d12 + your level.
Your puppet learns to cast one cantrip, and one 1st level spell, both from the wizard spell list(no healing). It uses its
modifier for the spellcasting ability and must take a long rest before casting the 1st-level spell again.
Your puppet's body increases in size in all dimensions, changing its size to Large. This functions like the enlarge/reduce spell.
Your puppet gains wings, jets, or some other way of flight, giving it flight speed equal to its movement speed.
Your puppet learns to cast one cantrip, one 1st level spell, one 2nd level spell, and one 3rd level spell, all from the wizard spell list (no healing). It uses its
modifier for the spellcasting ability, casts the three spells at 3rd level, and can only use each spell once before they must take a long rest to use it again.
Your puppet gains proficiency in all armor.

Your puppet's natural weapons improve further, growing stronger, harder, or sharper. Your puppet's unarmed strikes now deal 2d8 piercing, slashing, or bludgeoning damage. Your puppet can use dexterity or strength for these attacks.

Your puppet's body increases in size in all dimensions, changing its size to Gargantuan. However, to control this puppet you must be inside it, but you are under full cover, and the puppet's Hit dice is a d12.

As an action, you generate a large amount of cursed energy in the palm of one hand, blasting it at a target for 6 CE. Make a ranged attack with Dex + Proficiency + 3, This attack deals 20d6 Necrotic damage and recharges on a 5-6 d6.

As an action, you create 5 orbs made of cursed energy and blast them. Choose targets for each orb and make a ranged Cursed Energy attack with a +3 for 4 CE. On a hit, this attack Deals 6d6 Necrotic damage. Recharges on a 5-6 d6.

At 3rd level, you have begun to slowly improve your puppet. You will gain a Lesser Puppet and can summon it as an action for 3 Cursed Energy, though this Puppet can only have 2 Minor Traits and 2 Lesser Traits.

Once you reach 6th level, through the constant use of your puppet, you have begun to fix some of its downfalls. You will gain an Advanced Puppet and can summon it as an action for 6 Cursed Energy, though this Puppet can only have 2 Minor Traits, 2 Lesser Traits, and 2 Advanced Traits.

When you reach 11th level, you have perfected your puppet for its desired uses. You will gain a Master Puppet and can summon it as an action for 10 Cursed Energy, though this Puppet can only have 2 Minor Traits, 2 Lesser Traits, 2 Advanced Traits, and 2 Absolute Traits.
Finally, at 18th level, you reach the peak of your technique. Your manipulation is now no longer limited to puppets. You can now
manipulate the creatures in your domain like puppets in a puppet show.
At initiative 20, all creatures take an action of your choice that does not cost cursed energy.

Beginning at 1st level, you gain a +1 to critical range. Additionally, you roll an additional damage dice on a critical hit.

Once you reach 3rd level, you have learned your technique that creates weak spots in enemies. Whenever you hit an attack, you can spend 1 cursed energy to roll a d10. If you roll a 3 or 7 the attack becomes a critical hit.
You now roll 2 additional damage dice on a critical hit.

When you reach 6th level, as an action for 4 Cursed Energy, you make an attack to destroy the ground around you in a 30 ft circle, applying your critical hit to the rubble. The area becomes difficult terrain and every creature in the area must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failure, they take your attack’s damage + 3d10 bludgeoning damage. On a success, they take half as much damage.
You now roll 3 additional damage dice on a critical hit.

At 11th level, you have become more lethal and precise with your Ratio. When you use Ratio, you now roll 2d10 instead of one and you can spend additional CE up to your Cursed Energy modifier to roll an additional d10 per CE spent. You roll 4 additional damage dice on a critical hit.
Finally, at 18th level, you have honed your skill with your technique to a fine edge. In your domain, all of your attacks count as critical hits and
you deal an additional 5 damage dice on a critical hit.

Starting at 1st level, you can manifest your Regalia as an action for 2 CE for a number of hours equal to your Cursed Energy modifier. Your Regalia takes the form of a simple or martial melee weapon of your choice, such as Dagger or a Shortsword. You are proficient with the weapon and gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls using your Regalia. Once per turn on a hit you can spend 1 CE to deal an additional 1d8
necrotic damage. This becomes 2d8 at 3rd level, 3d8 at 6th level, 4d8 at 11th level and 6d8 at 18th level.
Your Regalia disappears if it is more than 30 feet away from you and cannot be wielded by other creatures.

At 3rd level, you have learned greater control over your Regalia. For 1 CE, you can make one of your attacks with your Regalia into a cutting wave of cursed energy. This creates a 5 ft wide 30 ft long line. Creatures in range must make a Dexterity save, taking the damage of your regalia in necrotic damage on a failed save.
At 6th level, the seal further loosens, granting you more abilities.
Your Regalia now has a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls. This increases to a +3 bonus at 11th level and +4 at 18th level.

Your Regalia now has a pool of hit points equal to 5 times your level. When you take damage, you can spend 1 cursed energy as a reaction to damage to cause that damage to instead target the regalia’s pool.

If this hit point pool is reduced to 0 hit points, you take any remaining damage and your regalia breaks and must be resummoned. When broken, your regalia can be resummoned a number of times equal to your Cursed Energy modifier. Otherwise, you cannot summon your regalia until you complete a long rest.
At 11th level, your control over your Soul Regalia has loosened nearly all of the seal. Your regalia is now a special grade cursed tool. Work with your GM to decide what its technique is.

As an action, you can spend 10 cursed energy to cause your regalia to hover for 1 minute. Your regalia has an AC equal to 12 + your cursed energy modifier + your proficiency bonus and hit points equal to its pool while hovering. The regalia is destroyed if reduced to 0 hit points. You gain the following actions:

As an action you can command the weapon to move up to 100 feet and can make any attacks on your turn originate from the Regalia as if you were wielding it. You can use your cursed energy modifier for attack and damage rolls for these attacks.

As an action, you can cause your regalia to move in a 100 foot line attack, appearing at the end of the line if it is a melee weapon. All creatures within range must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking your regalia damage on a hit.
After the minute is up, the Soul Regalia moves 100 ft towards you, attempting to return. If unable to, it falls to the ground.

At 18th level, the seal is completely removed as you have perfected a domain expansion that you put your soul into. The domain is filled with numerous types of Lesser Regalia in the form of random weapons. At initiative 20, the Lesser Regalia will attack any enemies within the domain, dealing 8d10 necrotic damage. Additionally, you can use
as an action without spending any cursed energy. In your domain it has immunity to all damage and you can use one of its actions once per turn as a free action.

Also at 3rd level, you can use this feature on a creature within 30 ft of you that you can see for an additional 2 CE. Other creatures do not gain the bonus to rolls.

At 6th level, you can spend 3 additional cursed energy to continue regression to the point you started your previous turn.

If your movement is blocked, you can force your way through. If your path is blocked by a creature, they must make a Dexterity save or take your proficiency bonus in d8s of bludgeoning damage and are pushed to a different space out of your path if their size is Large or smaller (your choice). If your path is blocked by a structure or object that is not fixed in place, you can make a Cursed Energy check to move it (DC 10 + 3 for every size category above Medium). On a success, you move it out of the way. Otherwise you take 5 bludgeoning damage and the structure or object takes 10 times your proficiency bonus in bludgeoning damage. If this destroys the object, you continue moving, otherwise you stop moving.

While holding an instrument you are proficient in, you can spend 1 CE as an action to play it and launch a Sound Blast at a target within 30 feet. Make a ranged Cursed Energy attack roll, on a hit you deal 2d10 thunder damage and if the target is a creature, it must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed back 10 feet. This technique's damage increases to 3d10 at 6th level, 4d10 at 11th level, and 6d10 at 18th level.

At 3rd level, when you use your action to launch a Sound Blast, you can launch up to two Sound Blasts, spending 1 Cursed Energy for each. At 11th level you can make up to three Sound Blast attacks as part of your action.

At 6th level, you have learned to apply your Sound Blast to an area. As an action for 5 cursed energy, you can launch a Sound Wave in a 15 feet cone. All creatures within range must make a Constitution saving throw or take your Sound Blast damage + additional d10s equal to your proficiency bonus and be pushed back 20 feet and deafened until the end of their next turn on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful save.
The range of your Sound Blast now increases to 60 feet. The range of your Sound Wave increases to 30 feet at 11th level.

At 11th level, you can spend 8 cursed energy to start a solo. For the next minute, your attacks deal an additional 2d10 thunder damage and if a creature fails its saving throw against your technique it gains disadvantage on its next attack roll or ability check.

You can also spend additional cursed energy up to half your proficiency bonus to deal an additional 2d10 thunder per CE spent. A hostile creature that ends its turn within 15 feet of you during your solo takes thunder damage equal to your CE modifier + your proficiency bonus.

Starting at 1st level, you possess toxic blood. You gain resistance to poison and acid damage and have advantage on saving throws against the poisoned condition. When you have less than your hit point maximum, you can cause your unarmed strikes or melee weapon attacks to deal an additional 1d8 acid damage once per turn. This increases to 2d8 at 3rd level, 3d8 at 6th level, and 4d8 at 11th level.

Once as part of a long rest, you can spend $100 and hit points up to your proficiency bonus to fill a Blood Bag with your own blood. This Blood Bag counts as a source of hit points for your Rot features. A Blood Bag lasts 5 days outside of refrigeration before it goes bad. You can have a number of Blood Bags equal to your Constitution modifier at once.

Starting at 1st level, you can harness your blood in a manner fit for battle. When you use a Rot technique or feature, you can ignore the HP cost if you have an alternate source of blood. You gain four techniques and two additional techniques at 6th and 11th level:
. As an action for 1 CE and 2 HP, you force a creature within 15 feet to make a Constitution save or take 2d6 acid damage and be blinded until the end of their turn on a fail.
. Once per turn on a hit with a melee attack, you can spend 1 CE and 1 HP to deal an additional 2d8 acid damage.

. As an action for 3 CE and 4 HP, you can make a ranged cursed energy attack against a target within 30 feet. On a hit, the target takes 2d8 piercing and 2d10 acid damage and must make a Constitution saving throw or have their movement reduced by 10 feet until the end of their next turn.

. As an action for 3 CE and 5 HP, you launch waves of your rotten blood in a 15 feet cone. Creatures in range must make a Constitution saving throw or take 5d8 acid damage or half as much damage on a success.

. As a reaction, you spend CE up to your modifier and twice that amount in HP. For each CE spent, the Blood Shield gains 10 hit points, which absorbs the damage and you take remaining damage. If this reduces a melee attack to 0, the attacker must make a Constitution save or take 2d8 acid damage.

. As an action for 4 CE and 5 HP you can shoot a seeking blood missile at a target within 60 feet. On a hit, the target takes 5d10 + your CE modifier in acid damage. You can reroll the attack roll using your bonus action or reaction.

. As a bonus action for 3 CE and 3 HP, you can coat your limbs in your blood. For the next minute, your walking speed increases by 10 ft and your unarmed strikes deal 2d6 + CE modifier acid damage on a hit.

. As an action for 2 CE and 3 HP, you form your blood into a spear. Make a ranged cursed energy attack roll with a range of 30/90 feet. On a hit the target takes 1d6 piercing and 2d10 + CE modifier acid damage.
for 2 CE and 3 HP, you pick a point within 60 ft. Creatures within 15 feet must make a Dexterity Saving throw taking 1d10 piercing and 2d10 acid damage on failed save or half as much on a success.

At 3rd level you have learned to use your blood infectiously. As a bonus action for 3 Cursed Energy, you can cause all creatures that have taken damage from your technique in the last minute to form black floral patterns on their body as they have been infected with your blood.
At the beginning of your turn, they take your Rotten Blood damage. This lasts for 1 minute unless you spend 3 cursed energy to continue the effect or end it as a free action.
At 6th level, creatures also gain the poisoned condition for the duration and Decay also reduces a creature’s hit point maximum. A creature’s maximum hit points return to normal after a long rest.

At 6th level, you have proved your mastery over your technique. Your technique now ignores resistance to acid damage and a creature that fails a saving throw against your technique is poisoned for 1 minute and can make a Constitution save at the end of their turn to end the effect on themselves.
You gain immunity to poison and acid damage as well as the poisoned condition. At 18th level, your technique treats immunity to acid damage as resistance.
At 11th level, you learn to condense your blood into wings resembling veins as a bonus action for 8 CE, gaining the following benefits for 1 minute:
You gain a flying speed equal to half your movement
You gain advantage on Dexterity saving throws
You can replace an attack on your turn with a Rot Technique or one line of blood attack.
As a free action on your turn, you can unleash lines of blood.

These lines of blood take the shape of three ranged Cursed Energy attacks against a target within 60 feet. Each attack deals 4d10 + your CE modifier acid or necrotic damage. You can also replace an attack on your turn with a line of blood attack. While using Wing King, you cannot use Decay.
Domain Expansion: Mind Palace of Corrupted Ego

At 18th level you have mastered your technique, allowing you to expand your domain. All creatures within your domain are under the effects of Decay and take additional Decay damage at initiative 20. Additionally,
your Rot Techniques use hit points from other creatures within your domain.

You can use this technique only if you haven't moved this turn, and after you use it, your speed is 0 until the end of the current turn.
At 6th level, you have learned to apply your cursed seals onto others, allowing for even more accurate and deadly shots. When you use a mark, any previous marks you have active ends.

As a bonus action for 3 CE, you can mark a target of your choice within 30 feet for 1 minute. If you hit the marked target with an attack, your next attack against the target is made at advantage. On a hit, the attack deals critical damage and the mark ends.
As a bonus action for 3 CE, you can mark a number of targets up to your CE modifier within 30 feet for 1 minute.

As an action, you can make a ranged attack and activate the marks, causing the attack to split and attack each marked target within range of your attack. You make a ranged weapon or cursed energy attack roll against each creature, dealing your normal damage on a hit and the mark ends.

You must have a small body part such as a finger of the deceased humanoid that you or the willing participant must consume.

You or the target of the seance must spend 1 cursed energy at the beginning of the target’s turns while the technique is active to maintain its form, with the technique ending once the cursed energy runs out. At 3rd level, you have increased the potency of your seance.

If you lose concentration, the ritual stops and you must start over. After you have finished the ritual, you or a willing creature within 30 ft can transform into the dead humanoid if the CR or level is equal to or lower than your level + your proficiency bonus.
At 11th level, when you complete Ritual of Resurrection you can spend an additional 5 cursed energy to cause the target of the Seance to gain one of the following benefits.
. The target gains the hit points of the dead humanoid as temporary hit points if channeling Physical Information.

Starting at 1st level, you can control your shadow and cast Minor Illusion through it in a 5 ft range around yourself.

You can also strike a creature through their shadow. When you make an attack roll, you can spend 1 cursed energy to target a creature’s shadow that exists within their space. If the creature is unaware of your technique, you automatically hit as they don’t guard their shadow. The target takes your attack in necrotic damage and you deal additional damage equal to your Cursed Energy modifier. This increases to twice your Cursed Energy modifier at 3rd level, thrice at 6th level, and four times at 11th level.

Your Divine Dogs last for 1 hour, until they are reduced to 0 hit points or you dismiss any summoned shikigami as a bonus action while within line of sight. As a reaction to seeing your shikigami reduced to 0 hit points, you can unsummon them and cannot summon them again until you finish a long rest.

Your shikigami cannot use actions on their own. You must spend a bonus action to command your shikigami or can spend an action to order them to do something more specific for longer, such as protect that creature, grab that, defend that area, etc. The number of Shikigami you can control at once is equal to half your level(rounded up).

Once you reach the 3rd level, you have gained access to your other spirits, and you must face them in ritual combat alone to gain access to them. As an action, you can summon an untamed Shikigami within 30 ft of you without spending cursed energy. Any creature within 50 feet is considered participating in the ritual. An untamed shikigami will be berserk (attack the nearest creature), but if you have defeated the
alone (not including your shikigami) and reduce it to 0 hit points, you can now summon the
normally as an action for up to 1 hour and can dismiss them as a bonus action. You can summon a number of
at a time equal to half your level rounded up (Divine Dogs and Rabbits each count as one entity).
If reduced to 0 hit points during a trial with multiple participants, you do not make death saving throws until all participants are unconscious.
reduced to 0 hit points dies and cannot be summoned again. A destroyed shikigami is eligible for Totality, with the exception of Rabbit Escape or Mahoraga.

If one of your shikigami is killed, during a short or long rest you can perform a 1-hour ritual to pass on the strength of one deceased shikigami to a different Non-Totality (other than Rabbit Escape or Mahoraga), granting it a permanent Totality form. When you make a Totality, they gain the following changes:

Their Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Wisdom, and Charisma scores become those of the creature who has the higher score. Then they gain a bonus to that ability score equal to the modifier of the creature with the smaller score.(Ex: Nue has 16 Strength while Divine Dog has 12, their Totality would have 17 Strength.) They also gain the higher AC of the shikigami used.
They receive the hit points of both creatures.
Their movement speed is added together.(2 with 30 would have 60)

They receive all features, traits, actions, bonus actions, reactions, legendary actions, skill, saving throw proficiencies, damage resistances, damage immunities and condition immunities from both creatures.
Their size can be either of the shikigami.
The CE cost becomes the higher shikigami + half of the lower shikigami’s cost.
Their CR equals the creature with a higher CR + half the CR of the creature with the smaller CR rounded up.(Ex: Nue's CR is 4, and Great Serpent's CR is 5, their totality's CR would be 7)

After calculating ability scores, the difference in the ability modifier of the original user of a damaging feature and the Totality is added to the amount of dice. For save effects damage, the score corresponding to the save is used.

(Ex: Mourn Tiger has a +5 in Dexterity and Nue has a +3. Mourn Tiger’s Dexterity Score increases by +3, meaning a +1 bonus to Dexterity modifier so you add 1 additional dice to the Totality's attack to the damage dice that use Dexterity as the ability modifier, changing Mourn Tiger’s bite attack from a 1d10+5 into a 2d10+6.) This increase only applies to direct attack rolls and saving throws.
As an optional ruling, your DM can choose to ignore Totality, instead having all shikigami come back on a long rest, rather than being killed and eligible for Totality.

. You can store objects in an extra-dimensional space within your shadow. You can physically place something into your shadow, costing no cursed energy. However you must spend 1 cursed energy to interact with an object in this space, potentially removing it. Everything in your shadow counts for your carrying capacity. Additionally, you can trap creatures within your shadow. As a bonus action for 2 ce, you can force a creature to make a Dexterity (Acrobatics) check against your CE save DC. They can hold their breath for a number of minutes equal to their Constitution modifier (min of 1) before suffocating. They can make a Strength or Dexterity saving throw at the end of their turns, freeing themselves on a success and appearing prone in an unoccupied space within 5 ft

When you reach 11th level, you can combine your shikigami into different forms. As an action, you can temporarily combine two of your living shikigami into a single type, granting the base shikigami an alteration feature from the other. You spend half the CE cost of the base shikigami to summon up to your proficiency bonus in altered shikigami at once, spending CE for each.

An altered shikigami has half the hit points of the base shikigami and you can reduce its size category by 1 to reduce the CE cost by 1. When reduced to 0 hit points, it does not affect the shikigami used in its creation and is not eligible for Totality. You cannot summon any unaltered shikigami while altered shikigami are summoned. If the base shikigami or alteration shikigami’s CR is 4 or higher, you can only create up to two altered shikigami with them at a time.

Finally, at 18th level you have learned how to expand your domain. Your domain is a huge shadow barrier, filling your surroundings with overwhelming darkness. Any hostile creatures that end their turn within your domain must make a Dexterity (Acrobatics) check or become restrained and sink. They can make a Strength (Athletics) check at the beginning of their turn to escape. The area is difficult terrain for creatures of your choice, and you are under the effects of Freedom of Movement within the domain.

While inside the domain, as a bonus action you can spend cursed energy up to your Cursed Energy modifier to create a number of clones of yourself equal to the CE spent. The clones have all your features and stats, but not weapons or hit points and cannot use Cursed Energy. Their hit points are equal to your Cursed Energy modifier and become a shadow puddle once reduced to 0 hit points. You can use your reaction to switch places with a clone when you are hit, making the clone take the hit instead.

Your domain allows you to summon copies of your shikigami to overwhelm your opponents. Whenever you summon a shikigami, you can instead spend cursed energy equal to the shikigami's cost(treat its price as if you were outside your domain) to summon a perfect copy of the shikigami. You can spend CE to make a number of shikigami clones up to your Cursed Energy modifier on the same turn. You cannot create copies of Mahoraga with this feature.
In addition, your normal Shikigami won't cost you Cursed Energy within your

3 cores, 1 body, you have different forms with separate powers.

Beginning at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.

Starting at 1st level, your cursed energy is gathered into a single core. As a bonus action, you can choose to enter a secondary form giving you access to a special ability for 1 minute. You gain one core option at this level:
When you hit with a melee attack, you can spend 1 CE to ignore resistances. If the creature is not resistant, they are considered vulnerable.
As an action you spend CE up to your CE modifier to launch a blast of cursed energy. You make a ranged cursed energy attack against a target within 80 feet dealing 2d6 necrotic damage for each CE.

As a bonus action, you assume this form for 1 minute, buffing your defense. You gain a number of temporary hit points equal to twice your current cursed energy. You can spend 1 CE at the beginning of your turn to refresh the temporary hit points.

As part of the bonus action you take to enter this form, you spend CE up to your CE modifier. For the duration of this form, your speed increases by 10 ft per CE spent and you gain a +2 bonus to AC. You deal an additional 1d4 damage for every 15 ft you move in a straight line before hitting a target with a melee attack.
At 3rd level, you can choose two more core options. You can only have one core option active at a time.
At 6th level, you have learned to specialize in one of your forms, allowing it to become semi-permanent. Choose one of your core options you have access to and gain its upgraded option:
Your strikes are imbued with unblockable power. Once per turn when you miss with a melee attack, you still deal damage equal to your Strength or Dexterity modifier.

Your cursed energy has become far more destructive. Once per turn when you deal damage with a ranged cursed energy attack, you add your Cursed Energy modifier to the damage roll. If you already add your modifier to the roll, you add it a second time.
Your body passively reinforces itself with cursed energy. When you take damage, you can use your reaction to reduce the damage by your Cursed Energy modifier + your proficiency bonus.
Your body has adapted to improve its swiftness. You can spend 1 ce to take the dash, disengage, or dodge action as a bonus action.

Your upgraded options are always active even when you haven’t entered a core form. Though you can not benefit from an upgraded option while in a different core option’s form. You can gain an additional upgraded option at 11th and 18th level.
Starting at 11th level, when you would be reduced to 0 hit points, you can choose to lose access to one of your core forms for 1 week to return to half your maximum HP.
At 18th level, you gain true understanding over your cores. When inside your domain, you are under the effect of all three cores.
The Vengeful Cursed Spirit technique involves the use of the spirit of one you care about.

Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.

Beginning at 1st level, at some point in time, someone you cared about died. Unable to accept their death, you unconsciously cursed them and created a vengeful spirit of great power. Once per turn, you can call a part of the spirit to your aid. By spending 1 Cursed Energy, you manifest the spirit’s claw to make an additional melee attack as part of your Attack action. This claw attack deals 1d12 slashing damage. At 6th level, the number of attacks increases to two, and three 11th level. You cannot use this attack during manifestation.
At 3rd level, your life is very stressful, being a sorcerer is filled with danger and trouble. When times of danger come, your Vengeful Spirit

may forcefully manifest. When you take damage above your level + your Cursed Energy modifier, you must make a DC 20 Wisdom saving throw. On a success, you can handle the strain and don't let your spirit out. On a failure, your Vengeful Spirit manifests itself to protect you, going berserk (attacking the nearest creature to you). It acts on your turn, is charmed by you and cannot move more more than 200 feet from you. Once per round, as a free action you can make a DC 20 Persuasion check. On a success it will stop attacking and unmanifest. On a failure, it will keep attacking until there are no creatures within 200 feet. They will always focus on the last thing to damage you and then the closest
creature to you. If killed, it respawns after finishing a long rest.
At 6th level, the DC for the Persuasion check becomes 15 and your Vengeful Spirit stays manifested for a number of rounds equal to your Cursed Energy modifier under your control before going berserk.

At 11th level, you have gained more control over your vengeful cursed spirit. You can now manifest your spirit as a bonus action for 1 minute, now obeying your verbal orders. You can summon the spirit a number of times equal to half your Cursed Energy modifier (rounded up), regaining expended uses on a long rest.

When you reach 6th level, you begin to learn about your innate technique. As a bonus action, while your Vengeful Spirit is in the world, you can command it to make a claw attack against a creature within range. On a hit it can extract the creature's DNA with a claw attack. You can attempt to replicate it by spending 3 CE as an action to make an ability check using your Cursed Energy score. On a success you can copy one feature of the Cursed Technique you have seen that is of a level that you qualify for and fill prerequisites (such as RCT):

When you copy a cursed technique, you can only spend the base cost the technique requires. No matter what you copy, you can only use the technique in its base form. For example, a maximum output hollow purple
would only come as a hollow purple. You cannot use different copied techniques at the same time if they are from different innate techniques.

You can have a number of copied techniques features equal to your Cursed Energy Modifier and can use them a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus before they disappear and you must copy them again. If you have a limb or body part of the user, the number of times you can use the technique is doubled. When you copy more than your limit, you remove a copied feature to make space for another.
In addition, you automatically pass the Cursed Energy check if you have already copied the cursed technique before.
Once you reach 11th level, the bond between the binding object and the Vengeful Spirit becomes stronger. Your Vengeful Spirit gains the following benefits:
Two of its ability scores will be increased by 2, and so will their maximum.
You will gain +2 to your CE score, including its maximum while your spirit is summoned.
Whenever it is summoned the Vengeful Spirit will gain temporary hit points equal to half your current hit points.

Finally at 18th level, through many battles and copies, you have learned how to expand your domain. Inside this barrier, you are allowed to use all of the cursed techniques you currently have for no Cursed Energy. At initiative 20, you will also gain one additional action, which can only be used to activate a copied cursed technique,
which affects all hostile creatures inside the barrier.

Starting at 1st level, you can harness your negative feelings into a usable source of energy, called cursed energy. These feelings can be harnessed into attacks or abilities. The number of cursed energy you possess is based on your class, some classes use a modifier that being charisma or wisdom (Player’s choice)
Your cursed energy DC is 8 + user cursed energy ability modifier + proficiency bonus.

Starting at 1st level, you are constantly filled with the hunger impulses that come with your technique. When you reduce a cursed spirit, shikigami, or cursed corpse to 0 hit points, you can use your reaction to spend 3 cursed energy to devour its corpse. For 1 hour you gain a feature, action, movement, resistance, immunity, sense, AC, Ability Score or other statistic from the dead creature’s statblock such as Cursed Energy Affinity (Cannot take legendary actions, Cursed Energy or Domains). You can spend an additional 3 cursed energy to steal an additional ability and can steal a number of abilities from a single corpse up to your Cursed Energy modifier.

When you steal an ability that does not suit your body (such as fly speed), your body changes to fit the ability (eg. growing wings). For the duration, you count as the creature type your stolen abilities come from. If you have stolen abilities from multiple creatures, you count as the one you have the most abilities from. You can have stolen abilities equal to your Cursed Energy modifier active at once.

At 6th level, you can have stolen abilities from a number of creatures equal to your Cursed Energy modifier +2 active at once and last for 24 hours. You cannot use different innate techniques at once.

At 3rd level, you have learned to access previous abilities you have eaten. As a bonus action you can spend 4 cursed energy to gain an ability you have stolen in the past and can use it for 1 hour. This does not increase at 6th level.
At 6th level, your stomach calls for satiation and gives you the means to feed it. The amount of cursed energy required for
Additionally, you have learned to use cursed energy to enhance the abilities of the devoured. You can use one of the following benefits once per turn when you use a stolen ability:
When you use an ability with a base cursed energy cost, the cost of the feature decreases by 1 (minimum cost of 1).
When you use an ability that lets you spend up to a certain amount of cursed energy, you can increase that amount by 2.
When using stolen movement, you can spend up to your proficiency bonus to increase it by 5 ft per cursed energy spent.
When using stolen AC and are hit by an attack roll, you can spend 1 CE to add your proficiency bonus to your AC against that attack roll, potentially causing it to miss.
When using a feature, you can spend 2 cursed energy to decrease its action cost by one (Full-Turn Action > Action > Bonus Action > Reaction).

At 11th level you have learned to draw the power of the devoured from your stomach and into your flesh. As an action you can transform into one of the creatures you have devoured, spending cursed energy equal to twice the Devoured’s CR (min of 1) or Level. Your statistics are replaced by the statblock of the chosen Devoured, but you retain your alignment, personality, mental scores, Cursed Energy and Hit Points.

You gain temporary hit points equal to the Hit Points of the Devoured. These Temporary Hit Points vanish if any remain when the technique ends. The technique ends early if you have no Temporary Hit Points from this technique left.

You are limited in the actions it can perform by the anatomy of your new form and can only use your cursed techniques if your new form is capable of forming hand signs and chanting. This form lasts for a number of minutes equal to your level + your cursed energy modifier. You cannot use or benefit from
Domain Expansion: Tomb of the Devoured

At 18th level you have mastered your technique allowing you to expand your domain. At initiative 20, you can regurgitate a creature whose corpse you devoured into an unoccupied space within 5 ft of you. The creature is friendly to you and your allies and acts immediately after your turn, attacking all enemies within your domain whether you command it to or not. If the creature was sentient in life, it is barely sentient within your domain as a mere husk of its former self.
All regurgitated creatures disappear once your domain ends.
