This variant rule serves to allow players to obtain cursed tools more easily, imbuing their innate technique into it. After a creature has imbued a weapon with Cursed Energy at least 150 times, while having spent the maximum energy possible every time, the most basic form of the innate technique will be imbued into the weapon, which will gain the following properties:
A creature can use said technique without spending Cursed Energy a number of times per day equal to the CE modifier of the creature who imbued the technique into the weapon.
The weapon is now considered a Semi-Special Grade Cursed Tool.

A creature does not need to possess Cursed Energy in order to use the technique imbued into the weapon. Each Technique Imbued Tool may have varying effects depending on the Innate Technique imbued within them.

Only the first maximum infusion of cursed energy performed outside of combat each day counts towards creating a tool like this, unlike in combat where all are counted as normal. Only one technique can be imbued within a tool and a creature can only create one tool this way.
Multiclassing allows you to gain levels in multiple classes. Doing so lets you mix the abilities of those classes to realize a character
concept that might not be reflected in one of the standard class options.

With this rule, you have the option of gaining a level in a new class whenever you advance in level, instead of gaining a level in your current class. Your levels in all your classes are added together to determine your character level. For example, if you have three levels in Wizard and two in Fighter, you're a 5th-level character.

As you advance in levels, you might primarily remain a member of your original class with just a few levels in another class, or you might change course entirely, never looking back at the class you left behind. You might even start progressing in a third or fourth class. Compared to a single-class character of the same level, you'll sacrifice some focus in exchange for versatility.

To qualify for a new class, you must meet the ability score prerequisites for both your current class and your new one, as shown in the Multiclassing Prerequisites table. For example, a barbarian who decides to multiclass into the druid class must have both Strength and Wisdom scores of 13 or higher. Without the full training that a beginning character receives, you must be a quick study in your new class, having a natural aptitude that is reflected by higher-than-average ability scores.
You gain the hit points from your new class as described for levels after 1st. You gain the 1st-level hit points for a class only when you are a 1st-level character.

You add together the Hit Dice granted by all your classes to form your pool of Hit Dice. If the Hit Dice are the same die type, you can simply pool them together. For example, both the fighter and the paladin have a d10, so if you are a paladin 5/fighter 5, you have ten d10 Hit Dice. If your classes give you Hit Dice of different types, keep track of them separately. If you are a paladin 5/cleric 5, for example, you have five d10 Hit Dice and five d8 Hit Dice.

Your proficiency bonus is always based on your total character level, not your level in a particular class. For example, if you are a Fighter 3/Rogue 2, you have the proficiency bonus of a 5th-level character, which is +3.
When you gain your first level in a class other than your initial class, you gain only some of the new class's starting proficiencies, as shown in the Multiclassing Proficiencies table.

When you gain a new level in a class, you get its features for that level. You don't, however, receive the class's starting equipment, and a few features have additional rules when you're multiclassing: Innate Techniques, Extra Attack, Unarmored Defense, and Spellcasting.

If you already have an Innate Technique, you can't gain it again from another class, unless you originally had Body Manipulation. Your Innate Technique counts only your highest class level(You would gain the features from your 3 levels of Warrior, and wouldn’t gain the Innate Technique features from shikigami). You can only use the Innate Technique features one at a time.
Similarly to Innate Techniques, you only gain the Cursed Energy of your highest level class, scaling with your total character level.

If you gain the Extra Attack class feature from multiple classes, the features don't add together. You can't make more than two attacks with this feature unless it says you do (as the fighter's version of Extra Attack does). Similarly, the warlock's eldritch invocation Thirsting Blade doesn't give you additional attacks if you also have an Extra Attack.
If you already have the Unarmored Defense feature, you can't gain it again from another class.

Emerge from the darkness, blacker than darkness. Purify that which is impure. As an action for 5 Cursed Energy, you cover the sky and the ground within a 2165-foot radius dome of darkness for 10 minutes. Upon activation, a dark, almost liquid-like matter drips down from the sky to form the outer barrier wall in the shape of a half-sphere. The curtain changes and the sky becomes dark despite the time of day, provoking any cursed spirits out of hiding. For each extra 1 Cursed Energy spent, you can add 1 additional minute to the curtain's duration and +10 hit points. Your curtain has a number of hit points equal to your Cursed Energy modifier times your level. This barrier has an AC equal to the caster's Cursed Energy DC and automatically fails saving throws. It is also immune to Poison and Psychic damage.
You have learned how to invade the barriers of others without breaking them. You gain the following benefits:

While outside a barrier, you can make a Cursed Energy check as an action against the CE save DC of the sorcerer who created the barrier to invade it. On a success, you can enter the barrier although the creator will know a creature has entered.

While inside a barrier, as an action you can make a Cursed Energy check against the CE save DC of the sorcerer to alter its properties. On a success, you can change the creatures allowed to enter or leave or other properties of the barrier.
Prerequisites: Must have the Clan Sorcerer Background

Unlike Simple Domain, which manifests its own domain to protect against a guaranteed hit, Falling Blossom Emotion shrouds the user in cursed energy to counterattack the moment a domain's guaranteed hit makes contact. As an action or reaction for 5 Cursed Energy, you surround yourself in cursed energy to make any attack or effect with a guaranteed hit nullified and deal no damage. This technique lasts for 1 minute, but does not affect attacks without a guaranteed hit.

You can also use this technique offensively while wielding a melee weapon. As an action for 4 Cursed Energy, you can surround yourself in cursed energy to prepare for an attack for 1 minute. As a reaction to an attack, you can make a melee weapon attack at advantage against the attacker before the attack happens. On a hit, the attack counts as a critical hit and deals necrotic damage. Once you make this attack, you must reactivate the technique to use it again. If your cursed energy or technique alters damage type, it can also alter this damage

As an action, bonus action, or reaction against being affected by a sure hit effect of a Domain, or seeing a Domain Expansion open, for 4 Cursed Energy you surround yourself with a 15 ft barrier for 1 minute. Within that radius, the sure hit effect of a domain is negated and deals no damage. Anyone of your choice inside the barrier is unaffected. The barrier has no effect on normal cursed techniques or others entering the barrier. It only negates sure hit effects.

You learn to prematurely create an incomplete Domain Expansion. As an action for 10 cursed energy, you create an unrefined incomplete domain 100 ft around yourself for 1 minute. This structureless domain does not follow you, has a refinement of 0, and has no barrier.

The domain lacks a guaranteed hit, but you gain advantage on technique attack rolls and creatures inside your domain have disadvantage on saving throws against your Innate Technique. Any effects of your domain are halved until you gain your complete Domain Expansion, upon which you can choose a different feat. When the domain ends, you experience
for 5 rounds. See Incomplete Domain (pg 451) in Rules of Thumb for further explanation.

As an action or reaction against an attack roll or saving throw effect, spell or domain expansion opening for 4 Cursed Energy, you surround yourself with a 10 ft barrier for 1 minute. The circle has an amount of hit points equal to your proficiency bonus times twice your Cursed Energy modifier. Any damaging cursed techniques, spells, or attacks that target you or targets an area that overlaps with your simple domain, will now damage the barrier instead, reducing its hit points by the damage it would cause. Any damage leftover from an attack or effect that would damage you carries over after Simple Domain is destroyed. Your
Prerequisites: Must have Domain Expansion, 400 Refinement points
Your refinement allows you to further empower your domain expansion. You can choose one of the following benefits:
If your domain has a passive effect that causes damage at Initiative 20, the number of damage dice are increased by your CE modifier.
If your domain is Non-Lethal or has a restriction, you can add an additional condition or restriction to your technique.
Your domain refinement enhances the technique imbued into the barrier. While within your domain, the CE cost of your innate technique features are halved(rounded up).
Your domain refinement has made your techniques faster. Your innate technique features action costs reduced by one while your domain is active (Action > Bonus Action > Reaction > Free Action).
Your domain has multiplied the output of the imbued innate technique. When a feature lets you spend up to a certain amount of cursed energy, that maximum amount is doubled.
Your imbued technique has been refined. While within your domain, you can choose one of your Innate Technique features. The damage dice of that technique increases by your CE modifier.
Feats related to your Cursed Energy in its pure and fundamental form, and how to utilize it.
Prerequisites: 20+ Cursed Energy Score and a Breakthrough

You have touched both the core of Cursed Energy and the hidden Cursed Energy within you. Your Cursed Energy maximum increases by an amount equal to twice your level when you gain this feat. Whenever you gain a level, your Cursed Energy maximum increases by 2 Cursed Energy.
Your Cursed Energy has massive reserves, making you become a cursed energy powerhouse. You gain the following benefits:
You gain a +1 to your Cursed Energy score (maximum of 20).
Your CE maximum increases by your Cursed Energy modifier.

Your soul is rotten, and your cursed energy shows that. As an action, you release your cursed energy and creatures within 100 ft must make a Wisdom saving throw against your cursed energy DC. On a success, they can feel your cruelty but are not shaken by it. On failure, they are frightened and receive one of the following detriments for 1 minute:
They hesitate to act due to your suffocating presence, their ability checks, saving throws, and attack rolls are reduced by your Cursed Energy modifier.
Your power makes them become paralyzed in fear, they have a disadvantage on your saving throws.

If the creature's CR or level is equal to or higher than your level, they make this saving throw with advantage. If the creature's CR or level is 3 or more below your level, they make this saving throw with disadvantage.
A creature can repeat this saving throw at the end of their turn. Once a creature passes this saving throw, it becomes immune to this effect for 24 hours.
Prerequisites: Must have proficiency in Perception

You have learned how to track down remains of cursed energy. You gain Expertise in Perception if you don't already. You also gain a +5 bonus to checks relating to sensing Cursed Energy and can sense cursed energy from 90 ft away.

As a bonus action while touching a weapon, you can spend cursed energy up to half your proficiency bonus (rounded down) to enhance that weapon. The weapon gains a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls for every cursed energy spent (to a maximum of +3) for 1 hour. This does not stack with a weapon’s bonus if it already has a bonus to attack and damage rolls.

When attacking with unarmed strikes or a weapon you are proficient with, you can use your Cursed Energy modifier instead of Strength or Dexterity for your attack and damage rolls. However, on a roll of natural one for an attack roll, you must make a Cursed Energy check against your Cursed Energy DC, or shatter the weapon as you overcharge it or take 1 necrotic damage if using unarmed strikes.
Additionally, you can spend 1 cursed energy to imbue it into an object for 1 minute, causing it to deal necrotic damage for the duration.

You can enhance your body with Cursed energy. While not wearing armor, you add your Cursed Energy modifier to your AC. This becomes half your modifier (rounded up) if you have a feature such as Unarmored Defense.

Additionally, you can use your Cursed Energy modifier for unarmed strikes in place of Strength or Dexterity. As a reaction you can spend cursed energy up to your Cursed Energy modifier and gain a bonus to a physical saving throw equal to the cursed energy spent. If you have Reverse Cursed Technique, you can also use this feature for mental saving throws.
Prerequisites: Cursed Imbuement or Cursed Enhancement

As an action while holding a weapon that deals slashing damage, you can spend 5 Cursed Energy to make a huge cursed energy slash. You make all creatures in a 15 ft cone or a 30 ft line make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a creature takes the weapon’s normal damage + additional damage dice equal to a single die of the weapon times your Cursed Energy modifier in necrotic damage. On a success, they take half as much (Eg. Greatsword with a +3 CE modifier would be 2d6 + 3d6 necrotic damage).
As opposed to simply forcing cursed energy into use for your abilities, you have become far more efficient in their output resulting in a dramatic boost in power.
When a feature allows you to spend additional cursed energy, you can spend 1 additional cursed energy. This increases to 2 CE at 6th level and 3 CE at 11th level.
Once per turn, you can increase the damage of an attack by your cursed energy modifier.
You can choose to shield yourself as a reaction, you can spend 1 CE to reduce an instance of damage by three times your Cursed Energy modifier.
Your cursed energy has taken on a unique quality, choose one:
. You gain a +1 bonus to your attack rolls and +2 bonus to damage rolls when using your raw cursed energy (such as cursed strike).

. You gain a +1 bonus to AC and your walking speed increases by 5 ft. As a reaction to an attack, you can spend 1 CE to gain a bonus to your AC equal to your Cursed Energy modifier, potentially causing the attack to miss.

. Pick a damage type other than radiant or necrotic. When a feature uses raw cursed energy to deal damage, you can deal that damage type instead, dealing additional damage equal to your proficiency bonus.
You have mastered the trait peculiar to your energy:
. You gain a bonus to damage rolls using raw cursed energy equal to 2 + your CE modifier (such as cursed strike). This replaces the bonus to damage rolls from your Cursed Energy Trait.

. You reduce bludgeoning, slashing, and piercing damage by your CE modifier and your walking speed increases by 10 ft. This replaces the bonus to walking speed from your Cursed Energy Trait. As a reaction to an attack for 1 CE, you gain a bonus to AC equal to twice your CE modifier, potentially causing the attack to miss.

. Once per turn on a hit imbued with raw cursed energy (eg. Cursed Strike) or a creature failing a save against your raw cursed energy (eg. Cursed Energy Slash), they suffer an additional effect. These effects stack up to your proficiency bonus (if applicable) and last a number of turns equal to your CE modifier:
Acid, reduces the target’s AC by 1
Fire, target takes an extra 2 fire damage from your cursed energy
Force, target is knocked back 10 ft
Lightning, the target cannot take reactions
Poison, target gains the Poisoned condition
Psychic, target gains the frightened condition
Thunder, target is knocked Prone and Deafened
Prerequisites: Proficiency in a Ranged or Thrown weapon

You have learned to imbue your cursed energy into projectiles such as arrows, bolts or any other type of ammunition or weapon with the thrown property. As an action, you can imbue a number of projectiles up to your Cursed Energy modifier, turning them into Cursed Projectiles until you finish a long rest. When using Cursed Projectiles, you make ranged Cursed Energy attacks instead of what you would normally use to attack with them, and you control their trajectory while in the air, making it so that attacks with them ignore half and three quarters cover.

Additionally, on a miss they will stay in the air floating for a number of rounds equal to your Cursed Energy modifier, allowing you to keep making attacks with them even after being shot or thrown until they hit a solid object or target. You can use a bonus action to cause each active Cursed Projectile to make another ranged Cursed Energy attack against a creature within 60 feet. You can control a number of Cursed Projectiles equal to your Cursed Energy modifier. A creature can attack your Cursed Projectiles to destroy them; they have 1 hit point and an AC equal to your Cursed Technique DC.
Prerequisites: 20+ Cursed Energy score, 15th level, Breakthrough

Your cursed energy manipulation is some of the best that the world has ever seen, it must take at least a couple of centuries for another person such as yourself to be born once again. You gain the following benefits:

If a feature deals damage you can reroll all 1s and 2s on damage dice. Once per long rest you can deal maximum damage on a technique you use. This does not include ordinary attacks from you or shikigami.

Once per long rest, you can use one feature that requires Cursed Energy. The cost of that feature is lowered to 0 for that use, if a feature depends on how much Cursed Energy you spend, it counts as if you used the maximum required. For example, Reverse Cursed Technique would heal 50 with a modifier of +5.
You have specialized in the intricacies of binding vows, causing you to understand their innate workings. You can now make a number of binding vows equal to twice your proficiency bonus.

You can set a recitation of chanting for one of your innate technique features. You recite your chant as a full turn action and must concentrate until the technique is released. If you lose concentration, the cursed energy spent on the technique is wasted. When you use the technique on your next turn after reciting your chant, it will be given the following boost:
Your technique will ignore resistances and treat immunities as resistance.
If your Innate Technique feature is an attack, it gains advantage on the attack roll. If it instead requires a saving throw, the target(s) make their saves at disadvantage.
Your Technique feature deals double the damage dice.
If your Innate Technique does not directly deal damage, you can choose the following options:
The technique can target an additional number of creatures equal to your Cursed Energy modifier.
You can double the duration of the Innate Technique feature.

If your Innate Technique feature that benefits from Chanting requires more than one attack or damage roll or save to be made, only the first gains the benefits of Chanting. You cannot use Maximum Output or Domain Expansion while Chanting.
The sparks of black have chosen you to receive their blessings. You gain a +3 bonus to your Black Flash range.
Prerequisite: Must be able to summon shikigami

You have specialized in shikigami and made it your life. Choose one type of shikigami you can summon to be your special. You have a number of Ability points equal to twice your proficiency bonus that you can use to increase the ability score of that shikigami (up to a max of 20). Additionally, you can command any of your shikigami as a free action on your turn. This does not let you command a shikigami multiple times per turn. If you have multiple shikigami, you can swap your special shikigami as part of a long rest.
You have undergone extensive physical training to gain the following benefits:
Increase your Strength or Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
When you are prone, standing up uses only 5 feet of your movement.
Climbing doesn't cost you extra movement.
You can make a running long jump or a running high jump after moving only 5 feet on foot, rather than 10 feet.

When you use your action to Dash, you can use a bonus action to make one melee weapon attack or to shove a creature. If you move at least 10 feet in a straight line immediately before taking this bonus action, you either gain a +5 bonus to the attack’s damage roll (if you chose to make a melee attack and hit) or push the target up to 10 feet away from you (if you chose to shove and you succeed).

When you are wielding a finesse weapon with which you are proficient and another creature hits you with a melee attack, you can use your reaction to add your proficiency bonus to your AC for that attack, potentially causing the attack to miss you.
You master fighting with two weapons, gaining the following benefits:
You gain a +1 bonus to AC while you are wielding a separate melee weapon in each hand.
You can use two-weapon fighting even when the one handed melee weapons you are wielding aren't light.
You can draw or stow two one-handed weapons when you would normally be able to draw or stow only one.
Hardy and resilient, you gain the following benefits:
Increase your Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
When you roll a Hit Die to regain hit points, the minimum number of hit points you regain from the roll equals twice your Constitution modifier (minimum of 2).
You are practiced in the art of crushing your enemies, granting you the following benefits:
Increase your Strength or Constitution by 1, to a maximum of 20.
Once per turn, when you hit a creature with an attack that deals bludgeoning damage, you can move it 5 feet to an unoccupied space, provided the target is no more than one size larger than you.
When you score a critical hit that deals bludgeoning damage to a creature, attack rolls against that creature are made with advantage until the start of your next turn.

Your martial training has helped you develop a particular style of fighting. As a result, you learn one Fighting Style option of your choice from the Heavenly Restriction class. If you already have a style, the one you choose must be different.
Whenever you reach a level that grants the Ability Score Improvement feature, you can replace this feat's fighting style with another one from the Heavenly Restriction class that you don't have.
You've developed the skills necessary to hold your own in close-quarters grappling. You gain the following benefits:
You have advantage on attack rolls against a creature you are grappling.
You can use your action to try to pin a creature grappled by you. To do so, make another grapple check. If you succeed, you and the creature are both restrained until the grapple ends.
You've learned to put the weight of a weapon to your advantage, letting its momentum empower your strikes. You gain the following benefits:
On your turn, when you score a critical hit with a melee weapon or reduce a creature to 0 hit points with one, you can make one melee weapon attack as a bonus action.
Before you make a melee attack with a heavy weapon that you are proficient with, you can choose to take a -5 penalty to the attack roll. If the attack hits, you add +10 to the attack's damage.
You can use your armor to deflect strikes that would kill others. You gain the following benefits, on top of Heavy armor proficiency:
Increase your Strength score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
While you are wearing heavy armor, bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage that you take from nonmagical attacks is reduced by 3.
You have trained to master the use of light armor, gaining the following benefits.
Increase your Strength or Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You gain proficiency with light armor.
You have martial training that allows you to perform special combat maneuvers. You gain the following benefits.

You learn two maneuvers of your choice from among those available to the Battle Master archetype in the fighter class. If a maneuver you use requires your target to make a saving throw to resist the maneuver's effects, the saving throw DC equals 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier (your choice).

You gain one superiority die, which is a d6 (this die is added to any superiority dice you have from another source). This die is used to fuel your maneuvers. A superiority die is expended when you use it. You regain your expended superiority dice when you finish a short or long rest.
You have practiced moving in medium armor to gain the following benefits, on top of proficiency with medium armor:
Wearing medium armor doesn't impose disadvantage on your Dexterity (Stealth) checks.
When you wear medium armor, you can add 3, rather than 2, to your AC if you have a Dexterity of 16 or higher.
You are exceptionally speedy and agile. You gain the following benefits:
When you use the Dash action, difficult terrain doesn't cost you extra movement on that turn.
When you make a melee attack against a creature, you don't provoke opportunity attacks from that creature for the rest of the turn, whether you hit or not.

You gain 1 body point that can be spent on a Body Improvement from the Heavenly Restriction class. You must fulfill any prerequisites before taking it and you use your total level for the purpose of fulfilling prerequisites.
You have achieved a penetrating precision in combat, granting you the following benefits:
Increase your Strength or Dexterity by 1, to a maximum of 20.
Once per turn, when you hit a creature with an attack that deals piercing damage, you can re-roll one of the attack’s damage dice, and you must use the new roll.
When you score a critical hit that deals piercing damage to a creature, you can roll one additional damage die when determining the extra piercing damage the target takes.

When you take the Attack action and attack with only a glaive, halberd, quarterstaff, or spear, you can use a bonus action to make a melee attack with the opposite end of the weapon. This attack uses the same ability modifier as the primary attack. The weapon's damage die for this attack is a d4, and it deals bludgeoning damage.
While you are wielding a glaive, halberd, pike, quarterstaff, or spear, other creatures provoke an opportunity attack from you when they enter the reach you have with that weapon.
Choose one ability score. You gain the following benefits:
Increase the chosen ability score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You gain proficiency in saving throws using the chosen ability.
Once per turn when you roll damage for a melee weapon attack, you can reroll the weapon's damage dice and use either total.
You use shields not just for protection but also for offense. You gain the following benefits while you are wielding a shield:
If you take the Attack action on your turn, you can use a bonus action to try to shove a creature within 5 feet of you with your shield.
If you aren't incapacitated, you can add your shield's AC bonus to any Dexterity saving throw you make against a spell or other harmful effect that targets only you.

If you are subjected to an effect that allows you to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, you can use your reaction to take no damage if you succeed on the saving throw, interposing your shield between yourself and the source of the effect.
You've learned where to cut to have the greatest results, granting you the following benefits:
Increase your Strength or Dexterity by 1, to a maximum of 20.
Once per turn when you hit a creature with an attack that deals slashing damage, you can reduce the speed of the target by 10 feet until the start of your next turn.
When you score a critical hit that deals slashing damage to a creature, you grievously wound it. Until the start of your next turn, the target has disadvantage on all attack rolls.
Accustomed to the rough-and-tumble fighting using whatever weapons happen to be at hand, you gain the following benefits:
Increase your Strength or Constitution score by 1 (max of 20).
You are proficient with improvised weapons.
When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike or an improvised weapon on your turn, you can use a bonus action to attempt to grapple the target.
Your hit point maximum increases by an amount equal to twice your level when you gain this feat. Whenever you gain a level thereafter, your hit point maximum increases by an additional 2 hit points.
Prerequisites: Must have Reverse Cursed Technique

You have learned to feed your cursed techniques with reverse cursed energy instead of normal. This leads your technique to have the opposite of its normal effect. Turning debuffing into buffing and inverting damage types, resulting in a
Prerequisites: Must have Reverse Cursed Technique

You have learned to offensively use reverse curse technique, whenever you deal damage to a Monstrosity, Undead, or Cursed Spirit with an unarmed strike or melee weapon, you can spend cursed energy to remove hit points from your healing pool adding them as radiant damage.
Prerequisites: Must have Reverse Cursed Technique

You have reached new heights with this new type of energy, becoming an unheard prodigy. You can cause a creature you touch to gain the benefits of reverse cursed technique instead of you and can use reverse cursed technique once per turn as a free action.
You can make an Intelligence (Arcana) check as a bonus action while viewing a technique in play to understand how it works. The DC is equal to the user’s Cursed Energy save DC.

When making this check, treat your Intelligence score as a 22. If you instead spend a full turn action (Action + Bonus Action + Movement) attempting to understand a technique, you have advantage on the check.
Skilled at mimicry and dramatics, you gain the following benefits:
Increase your Charisma score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You have an advantage on Charisma (Deception) and Charisma (Performance) checks when trying to pass yourself off as a different person.

You can mimic the speech of another person or the sounds made by other creatures. You must have heard the person speaking, or heard the creature make the sound, for at least 1 minute. A successful Wisdom (Insight) check contested by your Charisma (Deception) check allows a listener to determine that the effect is faked.
Always on the lookout for danger, you gain the following benefits:
You can't be surprised while you are conscious.
You gain a +5 bonus to initiative.
Other creatures don't gain advantage on attack rolls against you as a result of being unseen by you.
Time and effort spent mastering the culinary arts has paid off. You gain the following benefits:
Increase your Constitution or Wisdom score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You gain proficiency with cook’s utensils if you don’t already have it.

As part of a short rest, you can cook special food, provided you have ingredients and cook's utensils on hand. You can prepare enough of this food for a number of creatures equal to 4 + your proficiency bonus. At the end of the short rest, any creature who eats the food and spends one or more Hit Dice to regain hit points regains an extra 1d8 hit points.

With one hour of work or when you finish a long rest, you can cook a number of treats equal to your proficiency bonus. These special treats last 8 hours after being made. A creature can use a bonus action to eat one of those treats to gain temporary hit points equal to your proficiency bonus.
When you gain this feat, choose one of the following damage types: acid, cold, fire, lightning, or thunder.
Spells you cast ignore resistance to damage of the chosen type. In addition, when you roll damage for a spell you cast that deals damage of that type, you can treat any 1 on a damage die as a 2.
You can select this feat multiple times. Each time you do so, you must choose a different damage type.
You have a quick hand and keen eye when employing firearms, granting you the following benefits:
Increase your Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You gain proficiency with firearms (see “Firearms” in the Dungeon Master’s Guide).
You ignore the loading property of firearms.
Being within 5 feet of a hostile creature doesn't impose disadvantage on your ranged attack rolls.
You are an able physician, allowing you to mend wounds quickly and get your allies back in the fight. You gain the following benefits:
When you use a healer's kit to stabilize a dying creature, that creature also regains 1 hit point.

As an action. you can spend one use of a healer's kit to tend to a creature and restore 1d6 + 4 hit points to it, plus additional hit points equal to the creature's maximum number of Hit Dice. The creature can't regain hit points from this feat again until it finishes a short or long rest.

You can spend 10 minutes inspiring your companions, shoring up their resolve to fight. When you do so, choose up to six friendly creatures (which can include yourself) within 30 feet of you who can see or hear you and who can understand you. Each creature can gain temporary hit points equal to your level + your Charisma modifier. A creature can't gain temporary hit points from this feat again until it has finished a short or long rest.
You have a mind that can track time, direction, and detail with uncanny precision. You gain the following benefits.
Increase your Intelligence score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You always know which way is north.
You always know the number of hours left before the next sunrise or sunset.
You can accurately recall anything you have seen or heard within the past month.
You have studied languages and codes, gaining the following benefits:
Increase your Intelligence score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You learn three languages of your choice.

You can ably create written ciphers. Others can't decipher a code you create unless you teach them, they succeed on an Intelligence check (DC equal to your Intelligence score + your proficiency bonus), or they use magic to decipher it.
You are a dangerous foe to face while mounted. While you are mounted and aren't incapacitated, you gain the following benefits:
You have advantage on melee attack rolls against any unmounted creature that is smaller than your mount.
You can force an attack targeted at your mount to target you instead.

If your mount is subjected to an effect that allows it to make a Dexterity saving throw to take only half damage, it instead takes no damage if it succeeds on the saving throw, and only half damage if it fails.
Quick to notice details of your environment, you gain the following benefits:
Increase your Intelligence or Wisdom score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
If you can see a creature's mouth while it is speaking a language you understand, you can interpret what it's saying by reading its lips.
You have a +5 bonus to your passive Wisdom (Perception) and passive Intelligence (Investigation) scores.
You can prepare and deliver deadly poisons, gaining the following benefits:
When you use poison, you ignore resistance to poison damage.
You can coat a weapon in poison as a bonus action, instead of an action.

You gain proficiency with the poisoner's kit if you don't already have it. With one hour of work using a poisoner's kit and expending 50 gp worth of materials, you can create a number of doses of potent poison equal to your proficiency bonus. Once applied to a weapon or piece of ammunition, the poison retains its potency for 1 minute or until you hit with the weapon or ammunition. When a creature takes damage from the coated weapon or ammunition, that creature must succeed on a DC 14 Constitution saving throw or take 2d8 poison damage and become poisoned until the end of your next turn.
You have mastered ranged weapons and can make shots that others find impossible. You gain the following benefits:
Attacking at long range doesn't impose disadvantage on your ranged weapon attack rolls.
Your ranged weapon attacks ignore half and three-quarters cover.
Before you make an attack with a ranged weapon that you are proficient with, you can choose to take a -5 penalty to the attack roll. If that attack hits, you add +10 to the attack's damage.
You have practiced techniques in melee combat against sorcerers, gaining the following benefits:
When a creature within 10 feet of you uses Cursed Energy, you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against that creature if they are within range.
You have advantage on saving throws against cursed techniques made by creatures within 15 feet of you.
You have mastered techniques to take advantage of every drop in any enemy's guard, gaining the following benefits.
When you hit a creature with an opportunity attack, the creature's speed becomes 0 for the rest of the turn.
Creatures provoke opportunity attacks from you even if they take the Disengage action before leaving your reach.

When a creature within 5 feet of you makes an attack against a target other than you (and that target doesn't have this feat), you can use your reaction to make a melee weapon attack against the attacking creature.
You have honed your proficiency with particular skills, granting you the following benefits:
Increase one ability score of your choice by 1 (maximum of 20).
You gain proficiency in one skill of your choice.

Choose one skill in which you have proficiency. You gain expertise with that skill, which means your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make with it. The skill you choose must be one that isn't already benefiting from a feature, such as Expertise, that doubles your proficiency bonus.
You gain proficiency in any combination of three skills or tools.
You are an expert at slinking through shadows. You gain the following benefits:
You can try to hide when you are lightly obscured from the creature from which you are hiding.
When you are hidden from a creature and miss it with a ranged weapon attack, making the attack doesn't reveal your position.
Dim light doesn't impose disadvantage on your Wisdom (Perception) checks relying on sight.
Accustomed to the rough-and-tumble fighting using whatever weapons happen to be at hand, you gain the following benefits:
Increase your Strength or Constitution score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You are proficient with improvised weapons.
Your unarmed strike uses a d4 for damage.
When you hit a creature with an unarmed strike or an improvised weapon on your turn, you can use a bonus action to attempt to grapple the target.
Prerequisites: 16+ Cursed Energy score, Proficiency in Arcana

You have the unique ability to create cursed tools. The time it takes to make a cursed tool depends on the rarity of the item, and the rarity of item you can make is dependent on your level and you can spend 8 hours per day working on a cursed tool. After creating a cursed tool, you must wait an amount of time equal to its crafting time before working on another cursed tool. The GM decides the cost of any materials.
You have practiced extensively with a variety of weapons, gaining the following benefits:
Increase your Strength or Dexterity score by 1, to a maximum of 20.
You gain proficiency with four weapons of your choice. Each one must be a simple or a martial weapon.
As an action for 2 CE, you can cast Levitate. You can spend an additional 2 CE to force the creature to make the save at disadvantage.
instead reduces all damage against you by half your
’s maximum height fall damage dice until the beginning of your next turn.
As an action for 3 CE, you can give yourself or another creature you touch a 60 feet hover speed for 10 minutes.
Your proficiency with your technique and bond with Kaichi improves. You can summon up to two
horns at the same time as part of your action. This lets you make an additional attack with your horns.
Your proficiency with your technique and bond with Reiki improves. While your movement speed is increased by Reiki, you gain a +3 bonus to AC and don’t provoke opportunity attacks.

Your proficiency with your technique reaches a crescendo, and your bond with Kirin improves. Whenever a creature hits you with a melee attack while you have Kirin activated, you can force them to take fire damage equal to twice the damage taken.

You have improved your ability to manage information. While you see through the crows you don’t gain the blinded condition. You gain 10 ft of blindsight for every cursed crow within 60 ft of you that is not incapacitated.
You have learned from the opportunistic way of the crows. Once per turn when you hit a frightened creature with an attack, you gain temporary hit points equal to your level.
Through trial and error, your mastery over Bird Strike has reached new heights. Whenever you use
you can choose between either increasing the damage die size to d12 or to roll an additional d6 to damage a limb.

If used against an unarmed strike, it is treated as a limb damaging effect using the Limb Damage table. Roll critical damage with your weapon. If you deal the required damage, you break the limb. Either way, the target takes no damage and this feature cannot remove a limb.

Your GM may also choose to allow more unique weapons or items.

A creature that is pushed back and impacts a solid object or structure takes 3d6 bludgeoning damage. Objects and structures in range take maximum damage. A creature that fails their save against this technique has their maximum hit points reduced by the damage taken until they finish a long rest. If the creature failed their save, this damage cannot be reduced.

Cursed Energy is negative energy and the fundamental of cursed techniques. It can be used through direct manipulation or to power innate techniques. Your Cursed Energy maximum is dependent on your class and your CE score (Wisdom or Charisma). Expended cursed energy is regained on a long rest.
There are countless applications for Cursed Energy. Your GM can allow characters to use the following to allow you to utilize cursed energy in inefficient, yet simple ways.
. On a hit with an unarmed strike or melee weapon attack, you can spend Cursed Energy up to proficiency bonus to deal an additional d6 necrotic damage per CE.

. As an action, you can make a Perception check using your CE modifier to sense cursed energy or residuals within 30 ft. The DC equals the target's CE save DC if the target was trying to conceal their cursed energy. You can track where a residual trail leads and you are aware of whose cursed energy it
As part of a short rest you can spend up to half your maximum hit dice to regain 1 CE per Hit Dice spent.

Cursed Energy is produced by negative emotions. If you experience intense negative emotions, you might find your cursed energy responds to it. If you fail three ability checks or saving throws in one round.
If you lose half of your hit point maximum in one instance.
If you experience a major injury.
If you experience a traumatic event (GM decides) such as the loss of a friend.
Pacts made by sorcerers and given to them at birth. These pacts hold great power and even greater consequences on breaking them.

Binding Vows made for yourself and your character will be an agreement between you and your GM, you deciding what you are willing to give and the GM deciding what to give you. You can only have as many binding vows as your proficiency bonus as a rule of thumb but feel free to ignore this.

At the cost of holding back while on the clock, when going overtime you get things done. If you reveal your cursed technique to a creature that can understand you, you gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made using your revealed technique, as well as a bonus given by the GM that depends on their technique. This ends once combat has ended and you cannot reveal your technique to the same creature more than once or a creature that already knows your technique.
For every limb you give up the use of, you gain a +5 bonus to your CE maximum (no prosthetics).

You need to use your cursed technique immediately, but can’t meet the usual activation requirements so you make a vow to use it without them. You create a vow to immediately use a technique that you know as either a reaction or free action just for using said technique for this vow, all other requirements besides cursed energy cost are ignored.

However, you permanently increase the action cost of the technique by 1(free action-> bonus action-> action-> full turn action) and add an additional requirement or prerequisite to use the technique for all subsequent uses of that technique (an example of an additional requirement or prerequisite would be now needing Chanting to use the technique). The increased action cost or additional requirement/prerequisite from this vow will be permanent as the technique has been permanently altered.

You train for 1 hour preparing yourself to fight against a creature you know. You create a vow where you choose 1 creature as your "favorite enemy", after that you will choose one of the following benefits for your cursed techniques:
You have advantage on attack rolls against that target.
You reduce the target's saving throws against your techniques by your proficiency bonus.

However, any other creature besides your "favorite enemy" adds their proficiency bonus on saving throws against your cursed techniques(even if they already do), and your attack rolls will be at disadvantage against them.
Even if you take this vow multiple times you cannot choose the same creature multiple times.

You have a deep admiration and respect for someone, so much so that you can restrain yourself just to obey them. One of the members of the vow will be the "master" of the vow, while another will be the "servant". The servant will receive one of the following restrictions:
Their Cursed Energy' maximum will be reduced by a number decided by its master.
Their technique's range is reduced by a number of ft. that the master decides.(Cannot go lower than 5ft)
Their technique's damage is reduced by how many damage dice the master decides.(Cannot go lower than one dice)
They cannot use simple domains or barriers.
The servant will have this restraint until the master allows the servant to unleash its cursed energy as an action. The servant gains one of the following benefits depending on his restraint.
Their cursed energy maximum doubles(using the original value without the reduction), and they regain cursed energy equal to the cursed energy they lost.
Their technique's range doubles(using the original value without the reduction).
Their technique's damage dice doubles(using the original value without the reduction).
This lasts a number of rounds equal to the master's proficiency
bonus, after which this vow can only be used again after a long rest.
Requires a Sorcerer and Cursed Spirit
You can attempt to tame a cursed spirit, forcing it to obey you by means of a vow.

The cursed spirit’s CR must be equal to or lower than your proficiency bonus. You must spend 8 hours per CR to tame the cursed spirit, in 8 hour periods. During each period, you must make an Animal Handling check DC 10 + twice the CR. On a failure, you must repeat the 8 hr period.
Once you finish the process, the cursed spirit can be commanded as a bonus action. If you attack or harm the cursed spirit, the vow is broken.
Binding vows can be very powerful, especially if a player bends the rules while creating one. To help maintain balance, here is a list of binding vow concepts to watch out for:

A player might suggest a binding vow that can be activated or deactivated at will. For example: "I am a limitless user, and I want my blue save DC to be increased by my CE modifier, but it can only affect one creature at a time. However, I can turn this vow on and off, so I don’t suffer any drawbacks."

This undermines the entire concept of binding vows because the player isn't truly sacrificing anything if they can simply toggle the effects off. For this, you can enforce a rule that it cannot be changed until completing a long rest once the vow has been made.

A player might suggest a binding vow where their melee-focused character gains advantage on all melee attack rolls but takes disadvantage on every cursed energy attack roll. Since the character isn’t reliant on CE attacks, this is not a genuine trade-off and doesn’t qualify as a fair vow.

A player might suggest a binding vow where they increase their cursed energy save DC in exchange for a higher cursed energy cost. While this might seem reasonable at first, it can quickly become unbalanced. Depending on the boosted feature, it could lead to encounter-ending abilities with impossibly high save DCs.

A player might suggest a binding vow where they lose something in return for making their cursed energy feature immune to reactions. This should be an automatic rejection, as reactions are a core mechanic of the supplement, and removing them entirely disrupts the balance of play, and completely bypasses most of the defense mechanics in the supplement.

A player might suggest a binding vow that allows their technique to mimic a feature from another technique. This should also be outright denied because it often doesn’t make logical sense and can quickly become overpowered.

A player might suggest a binding vow just as their character is about to die. For example: "I lose all my cursed energy and fall unconscious, but my technique automatically activates, teleporting me miles away." This is extremely unbalanced and effectively acts as a "get out of jail free" card, with no meaningful consequences for the player.

A player might suggest a binding vow that completely ignores the rules of their technique. For example: Idles transfiguration transfigured creatures being primitive or limitless being only able to teleport once per turn. The techniques rules are there for a reason and would stay better if they weren't broken by a binding vow. However sometimes a vow that breaks your techniques rules can be made good if the downside heavily outweighs the benefits.

A player might suggest a binding vow that increases their domain refinement. Under no circumstances should a vow like this ever be allowed. Not only is it incredibly overpowered but it doesn't make sense lore wise, as binding vows can only be used to amplify a sorcerer’s physicals, their cursed technique, or cursed energy in some sort of way, and the refinement of a barrier is based only on your expertise in putting one together.

A player might suggest a binding vow that their character couldn't possibly know about. For example: A character that doesn't have a barrier feat or levels in the Support Specialist class, making a binding vow for a complex binding vow for a barrier. For example: I vow that my barrier is reverse triangle shaped and any objects with cursed energy imbued into them can't pass through it at a certain time of the day but the HP of the barrier is reduced by 30 every round and it's cursed energy cost is increased by half of the original cost, despite not having any advanced barrier knowledge.
Consequences of Breaking a Binding Vow
A consequence feared by all from the weakest to the strongest. All sorcerers follow one rule; “Do not break a binding vow.”
After breaking a multi binding vow, you lose any benefits from the vow, and either gain 5 levels of exhaustion for 10 days or a major misfortune falls upon you, rolling on the table below.
You lose a sense(D4: 1.Touch, 2. Taste, 3. Smell, 4. Sight)
You cannot use Cursed Energy for 8d4 days.
Your Innate Technique is confiscated for 6d4 days.
The punishments can be avoided if both parties agree to end the vow.
Events reached either during extreme focus or moments near death, you manage to glimpse the core of cursed energy. Breakthroughs take one of two forms.
Channeling cursed energy into an attack within 0.000001, you cause a spatial distortion where cursed energy sparks black. This event is called a black flash.

In order to land a black flash, you must land a critical hit. After landing a critical hit, you roll a second d20, on a natural 20 you activate a black flash. This causes the melee attack to deal triple critical damage, rolling 3x the dice instead of 2x and ignore damage
Wish whoosh, reverse cursed technique processes negative energy into positive energy by taking two sources of cursed energy and multiplying them by one other. Impossible to teach normally.

After almost dying, be it being reduced to 0 in one hit while at max HP, or failing two death saves and then rolling a nat 20. Those are moments where the GM can choose to bestow reverse cursed technique. Alternatively roll a d100, on a 90+ you gain Reverse Cursed Technique. Reverse Cursed Technique cannot be taught under any circumstances, not including extremely specific outliers like Soul Swap.

You learn to use your cursed energy in a completely opposite way, channeling positive energy instead of negative. You have a pool of healing you can use with your reverse cursed energy that's equal to 5 x your level x your Cursed Energy modifier. As a bonus action for cursed energy up to your CE Modifier, you can remove healing from that pool to regain hit points. You can also remove healing from the pool as a reaction to receiving damage once per round. For every 1 cursed energy spent, you regain 10 hit points, removing an equal amount from the pool. If you are suffering from a physical condition or injury such as a concussion or something else, one of these effects can be healed for every 10 hit points recovered with the reverse cursed technique. Limbs can be regenerated for 20 hit points.

You can use your Reverse Cursed Technique until your healing pool ends before getting burned out, during which you can't use RCT until your healing pool recovers. At the beginning of every two rounds, your healing pool recovers 10 hit points. Your healing pool automatically refills at the end of a long rest. You can remove maximum HP reductions from Soul Damage by spending healing if you have at least 6 levels of Soul Awareness.

The awakened state following a breakthrough causes a sorcerer to gain an increased understanding of their cursed energy. When a character lands a black flash or awakens reverse cursed technique, your DM can allow the following upgrades as your ability to use cursed energy improves dramatically (counting total Breakthroughs).
You have focused on the basics, allowing you to directly manipulate cursed energy to great effect.
. On a hit, you can spend up to your proficiency bonus, dealing an additional d8 necrotic damage per CE spent.
. As an action you can spend up to your Cursed Energy modifier to reinforce your body. You gain 5 temporary hit points per CE.
Prerequisite: Skilled Cursed Energy Manipulation, 4 Breakthroughs
You have perfected the basics of manipulating cursed energy, causing your effectiveness and efficiency to explode.
. On a hit, you can spend up to your proficiency bonus, dealing an additional 1d12 necrotic damage per CE spent.
. As an action, bonus action, or reaction you can spend up to your Cursed Energy modifier + proficiency to reinforce your body. You gain 5 temporary hit points per CE.
. When using a cursed technique, the base cost decreases by 1 (min cost of 1).
Prerequisite: Advanced Cursed Energy Manipulation, 8 Breakthroughs
. On a hit, you can spend up to your proficiency bonus, dealing an additional 2d8 necrotic damage per CE. Additionally, you can spend CE up to your proficiency to add to your attack roll.
. When using a cursed technique, the base cost decreases by 2 (min cost of 1).

Positive Energy is poisonous to a Cursed Spirit which removes their ability to ever use Reverse Cursed Technique. Cursed Spirits have an easier time healing directly with negative energy using Cursed Energy Affinity, but they are quickly overwhelmed by the difference in output.

When a Cursed Spirit would normally unlock Reverse Cursed Technique, they instead gain an understanding unique to curses. They gain a number of Profane Points equal to their level and gain an additional point when they gain a level. At any time, you can spend any number of Profane Points you possess to gain a Cursed Physiology Attribute. Each Attribute has an individual cost and can only be taken once unless stated otherwise.

You gain a +1 to an ability score of your choice. You can choose this attribute multiple times, but only once for every 3 levels you have (E.g. level 9 can only have 3 Ability Improvement attributes).

you have superior vision in dark and dim conditions. You can see in dim light within 60 feet of you as if it were bright light, and in darkness as if it were dim light. You can't discern color in darkness, only shades of gray. This increases to 120 feet at 8th level.
Whether you are quadruped or have strong legs, your walking speed increases by 5 ft. This increases by 5 ft again at 10th level.
You are a terrifying curse and a horror to behold. You gain proficiency in Intimidation or expertise if you are already proficient.
You gain proficiency in either Stealth, Deception, Perception, or Survival.

You gain a natural weapon that takes the form of claws (slashing), fangs (piercing), or gnarled fists or a tail (bludgeoning). Your Curse Weapon deals 1d6 + your Strength modifier of its damage type. This increases to 1d8 at 5th level and 1d10 at 10th level. If you have a different unarmed strike dice, you can choose to use that for these natural weapons. You can choose this attribute multiple times, but must choose a different option each time.

Once per turn when you hit a creature with a claw attack, you can force the creature to take a Constitution saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength or Dexterity modifier). On a failed save, the target bleeds and takes 1d4 slashing damage at the start of their next turn. This increases to 1d6 slashing damage at 10th level. You can spend 1 CE to make the extra damage necrotic. You must have the
attribute and choose claw to take this attribute.

Once per turn when you hit a creature with a fang attack, you can force the creature to take a Strength saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier). On a failed save, the target is dragged down and falls prone. You must have the
attribute and choose fang to take this attribute.

The bludgeoning damage of your gnarled fists become 1d8. This increases to 1d10 at 5th level and 1d12 at 10th level. Once per turn when you hit a creature with a gnarled fists attack, you can force the creature to take a Strength saving throw (DC 8 + your proficiency bonus + your Strength modifier). On a failed save, the target is pushed back 10 ft. If the target impacts a solid object or structure, it takes 1d4 bludgeoning damage. This increases to 15 ft at 5th level and the bludgeoning damage increases to 2d4 at 10th level. You must have the
attribute and choose gnarled fist to take this attribute.

The reach of your tail increases to 10 ft. As a reaction to an attack roll, you can swipe your tail to roll a 1d6 and add it to your AC against the triggering attack, potentially causing it to miss. You can spend 1 CE to add a +2 to the number rolled. This becomes +4 at 10th level. You must
attribute and choose tail to take this attribute.

On a failed save, the target takes 2d4 poison damage and is poisoned until the start of your next turn. The damage becomes 3d4 at 6th level and 4d4 at 12th level. You must have the
You gain a +2 bonus to ability checks to detect cursed energy. This bonus increases by +1 at 5th, 8th, 12th, and 16th level.
You count as 1 size larger when determining your carrying capacity and the weight you can push, drag, or lift.

. You have an additional arm somewhere on your body. The additional arm can manipulate an object, open or close a door or container, pick up or set down a Tiny object, or wield a weapon that has the light property. This does not give you additional attacks, but does give you a +2 bonus on ability checks to grapple a creature.

. You have an additional leg somewhere on your body. This leg gives you a +2 bonus on ability checks and saving throws against being knocked prone or moved against your will. Your walking speed increases by 5 ft per additional leg you have when you take the dash action.
You can take this attribute multiple times, up to a total of four times.

Your size increases by one size category up to Gargantuan. This causes a +2 increase to your Strength score and -2 penalty to your Dexterity score. Additionally, your unarmed strikes and natural weapons increase by one dice tier up to d12 (d4<d8<d10<d12). You can take this attribute multiple times with stacking benefits, but the cost increases by 2 every time.
You sprout grotesque wings that give you a 30 ft fly speed. To use this speed, you cannot be wearing heavy armor or carrying more than your carry capacity. If you also have the
attribute, you gain the Evasion feature while flying.

attribute, the cost of this feature increases by 3 points.

You have learned to store items within your body, which cannot normally be removed against your will unless you die. You can store objects that could reasonably fit within your body. Additionally, your carry capacity increases by 3 x your level. The total weight you can store in your body equals half your carry capacity.
You have countless grotesque eyes on your body. You have advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks that rely on sight.
You gain either a 10 ft burrow speed, a 30 ft climb speed, or a 30 ft swim speed. You can choose this attribute multiple times, but must choose a different option each time.
Your climb or swim speed can equal your walking speed if it is higher. Your burrow speed increases to 10 ft and becomes 15 ft at 10th level. You must have the

You have strong scales or plating that protect you from harm. You gain a +2 bonus to AC.

When you use Cursed Strike, you deal an additional 1 necrotic damage per CE spent. If a feature alters the damage type of your cursed energy, it also changes this damage. This increases to 2 damage per CE spent at 10th level.

Your body lacks a conventional structure. You can move through spaces as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing, provided you aren't wearing or carrying anything you cannot fit through. You also have advantage on saving throws against being grappled or restrained.
You gain 1 Physical or Skill Feat of your choice that you qualify for. You can take this attribute multiple times, but must choose a different feat each time.
You gain 1 Cursed Energy Feat of your choice that you qualify for. You can take this attribute multiple times, but must choose a different feat each time.

Domain Expansion is the most supreme technique of any jujutsu user. It is achieved by expanding one's innate domain with cursed energy while using a barrier to construct it inside a separate space. The caster then imbues their cursed technique within the barrier to complete the expansion, allowing them to deploy their ability all throughout the domain.
All domains are different from each other, varying in their hand signs or techniques. However, they all tend to follow the same base rules unless otherwise stated.

All domains require a specific hand sign for their expansion to be activated, taking a Full Turn Action (Action + Bonus Action + Movement) to activate. All domains cost 20 Cursed Energy unless specified, and trap all creatures of your choice in a 175-foot radius circle centered on you, creating a barrier for 1 minute. The insides of a domain expansion vary from user to user, since it's like showing your soul to your opponents. Outside of your domain, its appearance is of a giant black sphere floating in the air.

All creatures outside your domain will receive Xd6 bludgeoning damage(X = CE modifier) and be pushed to the edge of the barrier. They received an additional 1d4 bludgeoning damage per object they collided with as the domain pushed them. In case the domain forces them against a wall, they must start holding their breath until the domain is closed or shrunk. Your barrier has domain hit points equal to 10 x your CE modifier, AC equal to 10 + your CE modifier + 1 per 100 refinement, and is vulnerable to damage from the outside and resistant to damage from the inside. Work with your GM to determine the environment and terrain of your domain.

Even if the barrier or environment isn't fully formed, casting domain expansion causes the user's innate technique to become unstable for a short time afterward. Right after ending your domain expansion, you cannot use any innate technique features and gain 2 levels of exhaustion for 1 minute or until you land a black flash.

Domains that are expanded to be lethal are constructed within a barrier imbued with the user's cursed technique. The caster's abilities are amplified and any cursed techniques deployed within the domain are guaranteed to hit their target. This sure-hit factor is derived from the barrier's embedded technique, which is what makes this type of domain considered lethal.

While inside your domain radius, all of your innate techniques will be affected by a sure hit effect. No matter what your cursed energy attack roll is, it will be considered a hit. Creatures will automatically fail saving throws for your innate technique. This and any other effects of your domain only apply to targets that you choose inside it.

In the past, Domain Expansion was a more common technique because domains weren't constructed to be fatal. They only forced targets inside to obey the rules of the embedded cursed technique. In exchange for lacking a guaranteed hit, a Non-Lethal Domain has one of the following:
While inside Non-Lethal domains, no kinds of violence or harmful action is allowed while a condition is not completely followed through. After the condition is completed, the domain will end.

Because your domain has a peaceful condition, you cannot open it while another domain expansion is active, however lethal domain expansions cannot be opened as a reaction to your domain opening. You can use your reaction to open your domain against a lethal domain, in which case the clash is different. The domain with more refinement points instantly destroys the other. In the case of two non-lethal domains opening, the one with more refinement points will instantly win.

As with every technique, Domain Expansion gets better with refinement and specialization. A refined domain and a normal domain are very different, while in the second case, most semi-grade 1 or above sorcerers could escape, a refined domain can bring trouble to even special-grade sorcerers.

The longer you refine your domain, the more refinement points you have. You start out with 1 refinement point, which defines many things about your domain. Your refinement limit is 1000 refinement points, only the elite of the elite have ever reached said point.
The more you refine your domain, the more versatile you can make it. Depending on your refinement points, you gain the following:
Your domain will increase in its durability the more refined it is. Your domain hit points are increased by +1 per refinement point you have.

The stronger the barrier of a domain on the inside, the weaker it is on the outside. You have realized this, and have found ways to get around it. As part of expanding your domain, you can decide if you want to make your barrier have vulnerability on the inside in exchange for it being resistant to all damage on the outside. In addition, you can spend additional 5 cursed energy when expanding your domain to make it perfectly balanced, making both outside and inside have no vulnerabilities or immunities.
Through training, you have learned how to use your domain hand signs with more efficiency. Your domain now costs an action instead of a Full-Turn Action.
While inside your domain, your techniques are at their strongest. While inside your domain, your cursed techniques and domain damage if any have additional dice equal to your Cursed Energy modifier.
You have learned how to expand your domain so

quickly that almost no one can react to it. As part of opening your domain, you can make it last only until the end of your turn. The cost for this domain expansion is halved, and it cannot be reacted to unless the creature has a higher Dexterity score than your CE score. When opening your domain this way, all creatures are targeted by its effects, too fast to choose.
With great practice, you have learned how to make your domain last far longer than it normally would. Your domain now lasts for 2 minutes instead of 1.

You have learned how to utilize the power of a domain without actively using it. As an action for half as much Cursed Energy your domain requires, you can cover your body to "wear" your domain in order to neutralize cursed techniques for 1 minute. Once activated, you automatically negate any defensive technique, offensive technique, or spell that affects you, and you can bypass barriers such as infinity with melee attacks. You will also negate a domain's sure hit effect if you're inside one. In addition, you can not use your Innate Technique unless you dismiss Domain Amplification as a bonus action. Even if you dismiss it, for the minute you can reactivate it as a bonus action without spending the cursed energy again. This technique does not work against techniques on Maximum Output if the user has 51 or more higher refinement than you. If they are within 50 refinement of you, you have resistance to their technique, and if they have 51 or less refinement than you, you are immune to their techniques even if they use Maximum Output.

It is no secret that opening and maintaining a domain is a very complicated job, requiring lots of cursed energy quantity, practice, and refinement. You have refined this with training, reducing your domain expansion cost by your Cursed Energy modifier. In addition, you only gain 1 level of exhaustion after your domain.
Your domain barrier has become hard and quite

unbreakable, making escape or forced entry almost impossible. Your domain will gain immunity to non-magical damage from both sides, however, it will still be resistant to all damages from the inside and vulnerable to all damages from the outside. In addition, your domain's refinement points are doubled when calculating your domain's hit points.

You have found a method to make your domain take up less space while making it harder to hit from the outside. As a bonus action while on your domain, you can spend 5 cursed energy to compress it, making the outside become a small circle of 5ft. Inside, however, will be the same size. Attack rolls against your domain on the outside are made with disadvantage, while barrierless domains must use this feature to target your domain on the outside. This lasts until the end of the domain.

You have reached the pinnacle of Jujutsu, mastering domain expansion. You have mastered your domain hand signs and can expand your domain as a bonus action instead of an action. You can reduce your domain expansion's cost by your proficiency bonus. While inside the domain, techniques that use an action can now be used as a bonus action, and techniques that take a bonus action can be used as a free action. Your domain now lasts for 3 minutes.
If you have RCT and Domain Refinement of 750 or higher, you gain:

You have realized the complicated issue of Technique Burnout can be solved in a simple fashion. Substitute your brain for a new one! Whilst under the effects of Technique Burnout, you can spend 4 cursed energy as a reaction to regain your Cursed Technique and remove the exhaustion from Burnout. You must succeed on a DC 5 Constitution saving throw. On a success, you remove Burnout without major consequences. On a failure, your eyes and nose start to bleed profusely as you take 8d6 psychic damage and cannot take actions or bonus actions until the start of your next turn. The Constitution saving throw DC increases by 5 for every success, being reduced by 5 for every minute that passes and resets on a long rest.
There are multiple ways of refining your domain, from training with yourself to clashing with other people's domains. Below is to list of how to gain refinement points:

Probably the slowest method, but every little progress counts. Once per day, you can spend a number of Cursed Energy up to your Cursed Energy modifier to add to your refinement level. This Cursed Energy can only be regained the next day.

One of the quicker methods of refining your domain is to destroy opponents with your cursed techniques while inside it. If you reduce a creature to 0 hit points while it's inside your domain expansion, you will gain refinement points. The refinement points are only gained if the creature's CR was at least half of your level(rounded up).

Subjugate another with your own. If you win in a domain clash, you gain refinement points from your domain superiority. You can only benefit from this once per month and not against the same creature.
All kinds of barriers have a weak spot, domain expansions could not be different. You can only deal damage to a domain's hit points once you've found its weak spot unless you're outside the domain.

Breaking a barrier from the inside is almost impossible, even if you do find the weak point of the barrier you'll still be targeted by the domain's constant effects. To break a domain from the inside, you must find its weak spot first by making a DC 30 Perception check. On a failure, the target cannot find a weak spot. On a success, you will find the domain's weak spot, now being able to target it for your attacks. The barrier has resistance to damage when attacked from inside.

While breaking a barrier from inside is nearly impossible, breaking from the outside is a much easier task. You can normally target the domain with attacks. It automatically fails any saving throws, and is vulnerable to all damage other than psychic.

Sometimes, even though it may seem like a disadvantage, you can forcefully enter a domain expansion by creating a weak spot, generally a hole of some sort. After you have reached at least 1/3rd of the domain's maximum hit points, you can take an action to make a Strength, Charisma, or Wisdom saving throw to forcefully open the domain. On a success, you will form a 10 ft by 10 ft hole in the domain that allows you and any creatures to enter inside the domain while you are concentrating. The moment any creature enters the domain they suffer the effects of the sure-hit.
Two domains expanding at the same time cause a domain clash, a battle solely defined by who has the most refined domain and talent as a sorcerer.

When a creature expands its domain, you can use your reaction to expand your own domain as well. The domain battle will be defined by the one with the most refinement points, being the defining factor in deciding the winner. However, even if you do have refinement points to destroy the opposing domain it will take a number of rounds equal to the amount of refinement points that you have above the opponent's
domain. See the table below to see how much rounds it takes:

During a domain clash, the sure-hit effect of both domains will be negated. The domain clash creates a 350 foot area, where 175 feet of it will be within one domain's area while the other 175 feet is for the other’s domain. The loser's domain area will shrink by 15 ft per round passed. Once you break the enemy’s domain, your sure-hit effect immediately resumes.

Although an extremely unlikely scenario. When two Domain Expansions of equal refinement clash, they completely nullify each other, not being able to overpower or be overpowered, so it's up to the two sorcerers to maintain their domain while bringing the opponent's down. As soon as one of the domain casters reach 1/3 (rounded down) of their maximum hit points they need to succeed in a DC 15 roll with no modifiers to maintain concentration on their domain. On a success, the domain is kept stable and they can keep going. On a failure, their domain breaks, giving in to the opponent's, and they suffer the after effects of Burnout from Domain Expansion.

A battle of two domain expansions is already hard to describe, now one of three or more is simply chaotic. When three or more domains are involved, the rules are the same, with the domains with less refinement being destroyed as soon as the necessary rounds pass. The barrier is expanded by 175 ft per domain involved, with the weaker domains getting reduced by 15 feet at the beginning of each round.
You have refined your domain expansion to new levels, making it become a true work of art. This can only be achieved by experiencing a breakthrough after reaching 1000 refinement points.

When you expand your domain, you can choose to not set up a barrier and remove the time limit. Your domain expansion radius increases to 655 feet, and it has a center at the middle. Your domain cannot be destroyed unless you receive 1/3rd of your maximum hit points in one instance, in which you must make a Constitution saving throw DC15 + half the damage. On a failure, the domain is destroyed. Your techniques still have a sure hit effect, however due to not having a barrier your domain is much simpler to escape. Also on a domain clash, your domain effects and cursed techniques can target the outside barrier of the other domain directly.
Only specific features with limb removing effects use this table. Removing limbs requires double the required damage.
