After reaching 20 Cursed Energy score, you have learned to use Maximum Output techniques with the highest possible cursed energy channeled into them. When spending the most possible CE (minimum 5 before any reductions), you can spend half the cursed energy cost an additional time to amplify the output of your techniques, using one of the following benefits (rounded up):

The technique's range is increased by half its original range rounded to the highest 5. For example, a technique with 10 feet of range would become a 15 feet range technique. This does not work with touch based techniques.
One of the technique's damage roll’s dice is increased by half of its original dice. For example, a technique with 10d10 damage die would add 5d10 die of damage to the total damage dice.
The technique's attack bonus is increased by half of its original bonus rounded up. For example, a technique with a +7 to hit would add a +4 to hit. DCs increase by half your proficiency bonus.
The technique's duration increase by half the original duration. Eg. techniques that last 1 minute now last 1 minute + 5 rounds.
Another value of your technique increases by half its original.
If using Maximum Output on a shikigami summoning technique (minimum 3 before any reductions), you instead choose one of the following:
Increase the size category by 1 and the shikigami deals an additional damage dice in necrotic on a hit.
The shikigami's hit points increase by half its original value.
The shikigami's attack bonus increases by half your proficiency bonus (rounded up).

If you use Maximum Output more than once per round, you must make a DC 15 Cursed Energy check or gain a level of Reduced Output. This DC increases by 2 for every level of Reduced Output you have. Trying to use Maximum Output while you have a technique magnified by Maximum Output active also forces this check. The CE cost of Maximum Output increases by 2 CE per level of Reduced Output.
. This lowers the CE range of techniques (E.g. up to CE modifier or up to proficiency) by a penalty depending on level of Reduced Output.
. At certain levels, you are also limited by the maximum amount of cursed energy you can spend at once. If a technique’s base cost is more than this max, you cannot use it.
. Depending on the value of your Die Tier Penalty, this reduces the tier of any damage dice you use with cursed energy or techniques, to a minimum of d4s

. An Area Penalty reduces the diameter or radius values to 75% or 50% of their original value (rounded down, min 5 ft) as well as the range of any features. E.g. A Barrier cast with 8 levels of Reduced Output that would normally cover 100 ft, only covers 50 ft. A 50 ft blast would only be 25 ft, and so on.
. This reduces the duration of any cursed energy effects or techniques you use by 50%, to a minimum of 1 round.

. For overusing Maximum Output, not using Cursed Energy for 1 minute lowers any levels of Reduced Output you have by 1. If a technique has a Reduced Output Effect, it will list when levels of Reduced Output disappear. Upon hitting a Black Flash, you reduce any levels of Reduced Output by 1.
Requires interaction with a soul affecting technique, possessing a soul based technique, or being a vessel.

. You house another entity within your body, containing two souls at once. The first time you take Soul Damage, you can make a DC 18 Intelligence (Arcana) check. On a success you gain 1 Soul Awareness if you have none already. On a failure, you can repeat this check again when you take Soul Damage. Each instance reduces the DC by 1, to a minimum of 10. This cannot increase your Soul Awareness higher than 1.

. For every feature you have relating to the soul, you gain 1 Soul Awareness. Innate Technique Features gained from leveling up normally (not including feats) only count once if they are gained from the same level, even if the feature has multiple parts or sub-abilities.

. When you are directly affected by a Soul Technique or take your level in Soul Damage from one attack, you can make an Intelligence check (DC equals 15 + twice the level of Soul Awareness you currently have). You have disadvantage on this check if you have no Soul Awareness. On a success, you gain 1 level of Soul Awareness. This can only increase Soul Awareness once per month. If making this check while in The Zone, you ignore disadvantage.

. A creature with higher Soul Awareness can attempt to teach. With constant instruction the instructor can attempt the same DC check as Soul Interaction once per month to teach. On a success, the student can make the check. This does not allow the student to make more than one check for Soul Awareness per month.

. Once per turn you can cause a melee attack to count as affecting the soul for effects that require it to count as such. You can use this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus per long rest.
. When hit with Soul Damage, you can spend up to CE modifier in CE to reduce the damage by 5 per CE spent. You can use this twice per long rest.
. While physically touching a target, you can differentiate their soul from others via color or quality. If you are familiar with a creature’s soul, you can recognize it via touch.
. Once per turn you can spend 5 CE to ignore damage resistances when you hit with a melee attack. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus each long rest.

. You can now attempt to make a DC 25 Intelligence (Arcana) check to make a binding vow relating to souls. A natural 20 is not an automatic success. On a failure, you cannot reattempt for 1 month. The DC decreases by 2 per level of Soul Awareness you have above 5.
. All of your attacks count as targeting the soul for effects that require them to be.
. You gain a +4 bonus to saves against effects that would possess you or change/move your soul.
. When hit with Soul Damage, you can spend up to CE modifier in CE to reduce the damage by 10 per CE spent. You can use this twice per long rest.

. Once per turn you can spend 5 CE to cause an attack to ignore temporary hit points, damage resistances/immunities or effects that would reduce damage. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus each long rest. Replaces Soul Harming.

. Upon dying, you place your soul outside the cycle of reincarnation until you decide to rejoin. This prevents any resurrection, preservation, resuscitation, or techniques that would affect your soul against your will.

After a jujutsu sorcerer successfully fully focuses themselves, they temporarily enter a heightened state known as "The Zone". In this state, manipulation of cursed energy becomes as natural as breathing to them.
After achieving a breakthrough, you gain the Zone condition, giving you the following benefits for 1 minute (these benefits stack every black flash):
When exploring the world of Jujutsu Kaisen, it can be hard for the GM to remember most of the rules of this setting. Here are some rules of thumb to remember.

Grade refers to the system that ranks jujutsu from grades one to four, and special grade. It is used to categorize the strength of jujutsu sorcerers, cursed spirits, cursed objects, and cursed tools. For sorcerers, the grading system not only determines their strength but also their value as sorcerers. The higher your Grade the harder the missions, but the rewards will also be greater. Curses are graded by the threat they pose to society, but Sorcerers are graded by their ability to exorcise curses. To increase your grade to Second or First grade, you must be recommended by two First Grades (Teachers cannot recommend their students). You are considered Semi First depending on your performance. You must then complete 3 missions with a First Grade Sorcerer. Upon satisfactory completion, you increase your grade.
Lowest rank; weak sorcerers or spirits
Basic sorcerers; competent against weak curses
If you have a handgun, you can rest easy
Skilled sorcerers with good techniques and combat sense
Veteran sorcerers capable of handling powerful curses
Even a tank might be insufficient
Top-tier sorcerers or curses; massive destructive power

As with sorcerers and cursed spirits, cursed tools are categorized from Grade One to Four based on their power and potency. The higher the grade, the greater the advantage granted to the user in a jujutsu battle.
Simple or weak cursed implements; minor enhancements or utility.
Reliable tools with notable cursed energy; useful in combat.
Strong, well-crafted weapons imbued with potent cursed energy.
Elite-grade weapons used by top sorcerers; highly specialized powers.
Unique, immensely powerful artifacts; often one-of-a-kind and tied to history or great sorcerer.

Cursed Techniques are abilities fueled by cursed energy. If cursed energy is comparable to electricity, cursed techniques are the appliances that use that power to function. Different types include Innate Techniques, Barrier Techniques, Shikigami, and more.

Innate Techniques are unique abilities congenitally engraved into the user's body from birth and will show signs at around 5-6 years old. When an individual refers to their own personal cursed technique, they are generally talking about their innate technique. All Innate Techniques are Cursed Techniques, but not all Cursed Techniques are Innate Techniques. For example, Technique Burnout causes the Innate Technique to be unusable immediately after a Domain Expansion. During this time, you cannot use Innate Technique features or Feats. However, you are still able to use features that use cursed energy outside of your Innate Technique, like Cursed Energy and Barrier feats.

Inherited Techniques are Innate Techniques passed down to sorcerers in the same bloodline. While sorcerers who don't come from prominent clans can inherit innate techniques, e.g. Straw Doll Technique, those obtained hereditarily from the ancestors of the Big Three Families especially carry the title of inherited technique, e.g. Limitless. The Big Three Families have maintained their authority and prestige by passing down powerful techniques to their descendants. Therefore, a sorcerer with an inherited technique is guaranteed an important position in the family.

Inherited Technique users have the advantage of being equipped with a manual on how to use them. However, passing down a technique through generations also presents the issue of other groups learning how the ability works, along with its shortcomings.

Any ability that enhances your attacks should cause those attacks to count as magical for the purposes of damaging cursed spirits/shikigami or overcoming resistances. Features will have action costs and prerequisites to follow in order to use the technique. Such as Cursed Speech requiring hearing, Ice Fall requiring you to fall prone, or Dowsing Vibrations requiring both feet on the ground. Without these, you cannot activate your technique. Techniques using a range e.g. up to CE modifier or proficiency, require at least 1 CE.

The Innate Technique is carved into the brain naturally and channels cursed energy into specific effects like an appliance using electricity. However, if too much cursed energy is used, the technique can become overwhelmed and need time to recover. Even if the barrier or environment isn't fully formed, casting domain expansion or similarly taxing ability causes the user's innate technique to become unstable for a short time afterward. Right after ending your domain expansion, you cannot use any Innate Technique features and gain 2 levels of exhaustion for 1 minute or until you land a black flash. Innate Technique features for this purpose refers to the Innate Technique that the domain was imbued with. For example, after a Domain Expansion a Disaster Flames user could no longer use Ember Insects during Technique Burnout, but they would be able to use features such as Cursed Strike or Cursed Slash that are not Innate Technique features relating to the burnt out technique.

. Magical effects created by and relying on your technique that do not fall into the other categories will be dismissed upon entering Technique Burnout. For example, a user of Illusive Mirage will be unable to create their Cursed Illusions and illusions they have applied to the terrains or to other people will automatically end and have no further effect.

. Any ability that is active on yourself, another creature, or an item will automatically end once under Technique Burnout. For example, a user of Star Rage would lose the benefits of Virtual Mass Increase once they enter Technique Burnout.

. You cannot use your Innate Technique to summon Shikigami, Cursed Spirits, or any other while in Technique Burnout. However, anything summoned by your technique will continue existing but cannot move or take actions. Any abilities or auras they possess will cease to function and they are treated as if they are stunned. If they were flying by any means from themself or your technique, they fall prone. For example, a user of Centipede Shroud would find that their Cursed Centipedes fall inert onto the ground and cannot be used as their Shroud during Technique Burnout.

. Any item or effect that must be constantly maintained by you will lose the magical benefits it possesses and will fall inert. For example a user of Golden Hour would find that their Clock Hand will continue to exist and be used normally apart from its magical benefits (being Minute Hand and Hour Hand) which cannot be used at all during Technique Burnout. However a permanent Cursed Tool created by a Construction user is not maintained by you and would be completely unaffected by Technique Burnout.

. Technique Burnout is a terrifying thing that nobody can simply ignore. Even the strongest must accept the limitations of their bodies. Though some called the strongest can find ways to circumvent these limits. If you have access to both Reverse Cursed Technique and a Domain Refinement of 750 or higher, you understand domains and burnout enough to apply your Reverse Cursed Technique to this problem. Substitute your brain for a new one! Whilst under the effects of Technique Burnout, you can spend 4 cursed energy as a reaction to regain your Cursed Technique and remove the exhaustion from Burnout. You must succeed on a DC 5 Constitution saving throw. On a success, you remove Burnout without major consequences. On a failure, your eyes and nose start to bleed profusely as you take 8d6 psychic damage and cannot take actions or bonus actions until the start of your next turn. The Constitution saving throw DC increases by 5 for every success, being reduced by 5 for every minute that passes and resets on a long rest. This accounts for the immense skill required for such a feat of jujutsu and the dangers of literally tearing apart your brain and restoring it to force your technique to function.
You can instead choose to price “normal cursed tools” (+0-3 items) according to this standard:

Curses are created when cursed energy leaks from (non-sorcerer) humans as a result of their harboring of negative emotions. Cursed energy thus gathers in one spot, building up like sediment until a cursed spirit takes form.

Cursed spirits bodies are entirely made up of cursed energy. Their metaphysical existence makes it impossible for non-sorcerers or creatures without cursed energy to perceive or touch them. Living non-sorcerers who have been cursed can only tell they have strange symptoms without realizing a cursed spirit is behind it; however, it is possible to gain the ability to see a curse in a life-or-death situation due to the overwhelming negative emotion the person experiences and consequently high cursed energy they emit.
Cursed Spirits have the Invisible condition against any creatures that cannot see them.

Though Cursed Spirits are born from a build up of negative emotions, it is still one of the main tools against exorcising them. Cursed Spirits should normally not have resistance or immunity against necrotic damage since this is the main damage type that all characters can use.

Due to the unique existence of cursed spirits, any and all cursed spirits should be immune to non-magical damage. A sorcerer with normal, unrestricted Cursed Energy has unarmed strikes that are considered magical and ignore the immunities of Cursed Spirits and Shikigami.

As beings of cursed energy, they are fundamentally weak to reverse cursed energy which is positive. Cursed Spirits cannot normally have resistance or immunity to radiant damage and cannot be healed by RCT. Additionally, cursed spirits of 3rd Grade or lower should have vulnerability to radiant damage.

Cursed Spirits are made up of cursed energy and their strength depends on the concentration of cursed energy and negative emotions that give them physical form. Though being more powerful is usually better, the weak concentration does give low-level curses the special ability to move through objects.
Cursed Spirits of 3rd Grade or lower can move through other creatures and objects as if they were difficult terrain. It takes 1d10 force damage if it ends its turn inside an object.
Shikigami are monstrous creatures resembling cursed spirits that are conjured to serve as familiars for jujutsu users.

Shikigami bodies are entirely made up of cursed energy. Their metaphysical existence makes it impossible for non-sorcerers or creatures without cursed energy to perceive or touch them. Living non-sorcerers cannot perceive shikigami; however, it is possible to gain the ability to see curses in a life-or-death situation due to the overwhelming negative emotion the person experiences and consequently high cursed energy they emit. Shikigami have the Invisible condition against any creatures that cannot see them.

Due to the unique existence of shikigami, any and all shikigami should be immune to non-magical damage. A sorcerer with normal, unrestricted Cursed Energy has unarmed strikes that are considered magical and ignore the immunities of Cursed Spirits and Shikigami.

Though cursed spirits and shikigami are both creatures of cursed energy, they are fundamentally different. Shikigami are created by passing cursed energy through a medium, creating a different creature with different properties. Shikigami should not have the RCT weakness and if a feature or ability specifies cursed spirits, they don’t affect shikigami unless stated otherwise.

Shikigami normally cost some sort of action economy to control in combat. If there is no action listed, they can be controlled as a free action, dismissed as a bonus action, and act on your turn unless stated otherwise. A shikigami can only be commanded once per turn regardless of action economy, since a shikigami only has one action, bonus action, movement, etc.

Heavenly Restriction or a Heavenly Pact refers to a binding vow forced on a sorcerer's body at birth. This affects their cursed energy in exchange for limitations or improvements on their body. Though there are many different types of Heavenly Pacts, this section is for the Heavenly Restriction class based on Toji Zenin’s unique Heavenly Pact.

A player character with the Heavenly Restriction class has absolutely no cursed energy. They cannot gain or manipulate cursed energy in any way. If an item or feature requires the usage or manipulation of cursed energy, they are ineligible for it.

Cursed Energy can only be seen by those with enough cursed energy. Having no cursed energy, a Heavenly Restriction class user cannot view these phenomena normally. This can be circumvented with a cursed tool, such as the 4th Grade Cursed Glasses or a similar effect. A player that is aware there is a curse can make a Wisdom (Perception) check (DC 18 - CR) to attempt to find the curse. On a success, they are able to detect the curse through means other than sight, but are still treated as if the curse has the invisible condition.
In addition to being unable to see them, they are also unable to damage cursed spirits or shikigami without a cursed tool as curses
should normally be immune to non-magical damage.

A fall from a great height is one of the most common hazards facing an adventurer. At the end of a fall, a creature takes bludgeoning damage for every 10 feet it fell, to a maximum of 200 feet. The creature lands prone, unless it avoids taking damage from the fall. The bludgeoning damage is determined by size category. As normal, a creature falls at a rate of 500 feet per round. Though a DM can choose to amend this metric.

. When a Medium or smaller creature or object falls onto a Medium or smaller creature, they must make a DC 15 Dexterity saving throw to avoid it. The DC increases by 2 for every size category the falling creature/object is larger than the creature.
. If a creature falls on a creature and the target fails their save, the fall damage is split between the two creatures.

. If a solid object (like a giant truck) is falling on a creature and the target fails their save, the creature takes the entire fall damage. A fragile object (like a glass ornament) can be ruled as using the Creature on Creature rules, with the fragile object absorbing part of the damage. If an object is at least Large size category and two or more size categories larger than the target, the target takes half as much damage on a successful save and is knocked prone and restrained under the object on a failed save.
. A non-mobile object automatically fails any Dexterity saving throws since it is an object. Determining which
object takes full, half, or none of the fall damage depending on the fragility of both objects (generally Fragile, Neutral, or Solid).

On your turn, you can move a distance up to your speed and take one action. You decide whether to move first or take your action first. Your speed, sometimes called your walking speed, is noted on your character sheet. The most common actions you can take are usually things such as Attack, Dodge, Dash, Hide, Search, Ready, etc. Many class features and other abilities provide additional options for your action.

. Various class features, techniques, and other abilities let you take an additional action on your turn called a bonus action. The Sharp Eyes feature, for example, allows a Scout to take a bonus action. You can take a bonus action only when a special ability, spell, or other feature of the game states that you can do something as a bonus action. You otherwise don’t have a bonus action to take.
You can take only one bonus action on your turn, so you must choose which bonus action to use when you have more than one available.

You choose when to take a bonus action during your turn, unless the bonus action’s timing is specified, and anything that deprives you of your ability to take actions also prevents you from taking a bonus action.

. Your turn can include a variety of flourishes that require neither your action nor your move. You can communicate however you are able, through brief utterances and gestures, as you take your turn. If a feature allows you to do something as a free action, it does not consume your action or bonus action. You can take only one free action on your turn, so you must choose which free action to use when you have more than one available. Certain features allow you to cancel abilities or features listed as (no action required). This does not consume your free action.

. You can also interact with one object or feature of the environment for free, during either your move or your action. For example, you could open a door during your move as you stride toward a foe, or you could draw your weapon as part of the same action you use to attack. If you want to interact with a second object, you need to use your action. Some cursed tools and other special objects always require an action to use, as stated in their descriptions. The GM might require you to use an action for any of these activities when it needs special care or when it presents an unusual obstacle. For instance, the GM could reasonably expect you to use an action to open
a stuck door or turn a crank to lower a drawbridge.

. Certain special abilities, techniques, and situations allow you to take a special action called a reaction. A reaction is an instant response to a trigger of some kind, which can occur on your turn or on someone else’s. The opportunity attack is the most common type of reaction. When you take a reaction, you can’t take another one until the start of your next turn. If the reaction interrupts another creature’s turn, that creature can continue its turn right after the reaction
. A Full Turn Action is a term that is relatively unique to this supplement. The basic Full-Turn Action is used for an especially powerful ability that requires your absolute focus, such as

. Unless otherwise stated, a Full Turn Action consumes your Action, Bonus Action, and all of your movement. If you have used any of these, you cannot use a Full Turn Action. Certain features have different Full Turn Actions, such as the
feat which allows a lesser Full Turn Action consuming only your Action and Bonus Action to analyze a technique. There are also features that can turn certain abilities into Full Turn Actions, such as
, increasing the action cost in exchange for

. The most common action to take in combat is the Attack action, whether you are swinging a sword, firing an arrow from a bow, or brawling with your fists. With this action, you make one melee or ranged attack. Certain features, such as the Extra Attack feature of the warrior, allow you to make more than one attack with this action.
Whether you’re striking with a melee weapon or firing a weapon at range.
. Pick a target within your attack’s range: a creature, an object, or a location.

. The GM determines whether the target has cover and whether you have advantage or disadvantage against the target. In addition, techniques, special abilities, and other effects can apply penalties or bonuses to your attack roll.
. You make the attack roll. On a hit, you roll damage, unless the particular attack has rules that specify otherwise. Some attacks cause special effects in addition to or instead of damage.
If there’s ever any question whether something you’re doing counts as an attack, the rule is simple: if you’re making an attack roll, you’re making an attack.

. When you take the Dash action, you gain extra movement for the current turn. The increase equals your speed, after applying any modifiers. With a speed of 30 feet, for example, you can move up to 60 feet on your turn if you dash. Any increase or decrease to your speed changes this additional movement by the same amount. If your speed of 30 feet is reduced to 15 feet, for instance, you can move up to 30 feet this turn if you dash.
. If you take the Disengage action, your movement doesn’t provoke opportunity attacks for the rest of the turn.

. When you take the Dodge action, you focus entirely on avoiding attacks. Until the start of your next turn, any attack roll made against you has disadvantage if you can see the attacker, and you make Dexterity saving throws with advantage. You lose this benefit if you are incapacitated or if your speed drops to 0.

. When you take the Search action, you devote your attention to finding something. Depending on the nature of your search, the GM might have you make a Wisdom (Perception) check or an Intelligence (Investigation) check. This is the action taken to find sneaking creatures, hidden entrances, or difficult to spot things. For detecting cursed energy, make a Cursed Energy (Perception) check.

. You can lend your aid to another creature in the completion of a task. When you take the Help action, the creature you aid gains advantage on the next ability check it makes to perform the task you are helping with, provided that it makes the check before the start of your next turn. Alternatively, you can aid a friendly creature in attacking a creature within 5 feet of you. You feint, distract the target, or in some other way team up to make your ally’s attack more effective. If your ally attacks the target before your next turn, the first attack roll is made with advantage.

. When you take the Hide action, you make a Dexterity (Stealth) check in an attempt to hide, following the rules for hiding. If you succeed against passive Perception, you are hidden from that creature. To prevent other creatures from detecting your cursed energy, you must take the Hide action but instead make a Cursed Energy (Stealth) check.

When you attack a target that you can’t see, you have disadvantage on the attack roll. This is true whether you’re guessing the target’s location or you’re targeting a creature you can hear but not see. If the target isn’t in the location you targeted, you automatically miss, but the GM typically just says that the attack missed, not whether you guessed the target’s location correctly. When a creature can’t see you, you have advantage on attack rolls against it. If you are hidden (both unseen and unheard) when you make an attack, you give away your location when the attack hits or misses.

. Sometimes you want to get the jump on a foe or wait for a particular circumstance before you act. To do so, you can take the Ready action on your turn, which lets you act using your reaction before the start of your next turn. First, you decide what perceivable circumstance will trigger your reaction. Then, you choose the action you will take in response to that trigger, or you choose to move up to your speed in response to it. Examples include “If the cultist steps on the trapdoor, I’ll pull the lever that opens it,” and “If the curse steps next to me, I move away.” When the trigger occurs, you can either take your reaction right after the trigger finishes or ignore the trigger. Remember that you can take only one reaction per round.

When you ready a technique, you cast it as normal but hold its energy, which you release with your reaction when the trigger occurs. To be readied, a technique must have a casting time of 1 action, and holding onto the technique's energy requires concentration. If your concentration is broken, the technique dissipates without taking effect. For example, if you are concentrating on Comedy (from Comedian) and ready Powerful Punchline, Comedy ends, and if you take damage before you release Powerful Punchline with your reaction, your concentration might be broken.

. Sorcerers and many curses have access to techniques and can use them to great effect in combat. Each technique has a casting time, which specifies whether the caster must use an action, a reaction, minutes, or even hours to cast the spell. Casting a spell is, therefore, not necessarily an action. Most spells do have a casting time of 1 action, so a sorcerer often uses his or her action in combat to cast such a spell.

. You normally interact with an object while doing something else, such as when you draw a sword as part of an attack. When an object requires your action for its use, you take the Use Object action. This action is also useful when you want to interact with more than one object on your turn.
Barriers are zones or territories established with jujutsu sorcery used to conceal, contain, or deny entry to entities within that space. Cursed techniques that erect barriers are known as barrier
. Certain barrier techniques are non-physical and therefore do not physically stop creatures or objects from entering the area of the technique. Relevant examples are
that despite being barrier techniques, do not physically exist or prevent entry/exit from the area.
. Certain barrier techniques create a physical barrier that stops creatures or objects from entering the area of the technique. Relevant examples are

which both create physical barriers that prevent entry/exit from an area. These physical barriers will typically have an AC and hit points and can be targeted by attacks and relevant techniques. If a feature deals additional damage or has some other added benefit when attacking or dealing damage to objects or structures, these benefits apply when used on a

The Reincarnated race is meant to represent the unique interaction between a vessel and a reincarnated sorcerer that has assumed a new form beyond death. When creating such a character, there are usually two options you can choose from.
You took in a cursed object holding the power and memories of a sorcerer or creature of ages past. You managed to resist their soul and maintain control of your body.

At times, the soul within your body may attempt to take control as determined by your DM and act accordingly. Whether this is a deadly situation when you are reduced to 0 hit points or a moment where the Reincarnated Sorcerer thinks they can take advantage, moments like these should be used sparingly, but kept as a looming threat if you decide upon that route. During such times, the Reincarnated Sorcerer can force the vessel to make a Charisma Saving throw with a DC dependent on the strength of the soul (DC 15-30). While the Reincarnated has control of your body, they act as an NPC controlled by the DM. They have access to both their Innate Technique and the Vessel's (if they have one), but can only use one Innate Technique at a time, not both.

You forced your soul into a cursed object using a forbidden technique and reincarnated into a vessel in the present. You have overwritten the soul of the vessel and taken eternal control of their body.
If you choose this option, you should have more knowledge on the history of this world depending on the time period you were alive. There could be secrets that other players do not have access to or
lore that is more readily available to you than others with skill checks.

Domain Expansion is an advanced barrier technique and is considered the pinnacle of jujutsu sorcery. It manifests the user's innate domain into reality inside a barrier infused with their innate cursed technique. Within a domain expansion, the user's innate techniques are improved and any that are activated are guaranteed to hit.

Your domain is the ultimate expression of your innate technique which is unique to you as a person. You and your GM determine the terrain of your domain. This cannot be changed later unless the GM thinks you have undergone a significant change to your character as a person.

The domain's guaranteed hit is one of the most important aspects of a domain. Unless stated otherwise, a domain functions as stated in the Lethal Domains section (page 421). A GM can allow a normally Lethal Domain to instead function as a Non-Lethal Domain by changing your Domain with a Binding Vow. Additional benefits of a domain generally fall under:
. A damaging Environmental Effect happens without saves and is part of the domain’s Guaranteed Hit that would be blocked by Anti-Domain techniques like Hollow Wicker Basket.

A Simple Domain is a tool specifically made to fight against Domain Expansions. Any creature within a Simple Domain is unaffected by a domain's guaranteed hit effect that deals damage until the Simple Domain is broken. If a guaranteed hit would deal damage, it instead damages the barrier. If multiple creatures are within a single Simple Domain and are targeted by a damaging area effect, it takes the

Innate domains that are expanded using only cursed energy without an embedded cursed technique are incomplete even if they include a barrier. Fully integrating the embedded technique into a domain is very difficult and enables its sure hit effect. Without that, the caster will only receive an improved cursed technique without a sure-hit effect. Incomplete Domains have refinement of 0 and that cannot change no matter what. A Domain's refinement is a measure of how well you can imbue your technique into a barrier. An Incomplete Domain user is completely unable to imbue their technique into a barrier, hence why it is incomplete.
of the normal Domain Expansion, an Incomplete Domain has the
. You gain advantage on Cursed Energy attack rolls and creatures inside your domain have disadvantage on saving throws as long as these effects are from your Innate Technique.

Unlike a normal Domain Expansion that inflicts Technique Burnout for 1 minute, an Incomplete Domain takes less effort and is therefore less taxing, only inflicting Technique Burnout for 5 rounds or 30 seconds if out of combat.

Barriers forcibly enclosed using the shape of an outside environment also do not incorporate sure-hit effects. So simply making a random barrier or using objects around you to contain your incomplete domain will not allow it to function as a true domain as the technique is not properly imbued into a barrier. Though it would allow the Incomplete Domain to close. A creature attempting to leave a closed Incomplete Domain must succeed a DC 20 Perception check to find the edge of your Incomplete Domain. After which they would be able to target the barrier or objects used to keep the Incomplete Domain closed with their attacks. Unlike a normal Domain Expansion, the HP and AC of the closed Incomplete Domain use the statistics of the other
Barrier or Objects used and not a domain barrier.

Additional benefits of a domain generally fall under: Environmental Effect or Technique Improvement. A damaging Environmental Effect will normally happen without a save and is part of the domain’s Guaranteed Hit that would be blocked by Anti-Domain techniques like Hollow Wicker Basket. However within an Incomplete Domain lacking a guaranteed hit, it will instead force a saving throw that is **not** affected by the disadvantage normally forced by the Incomplete Domain. On a failed save, they suffer half the normal damage they would take if this were a complete domain or suffer other effects at half effectiveness as applicable. For example, the Domain of Star Rage's: Event Horizon would normally deal 8d8 force damage and knock a creature prone without a save at initiative 20. In an Incomplete Domain, the creature would be forced to make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save they would take 4d8 force damage and fall prone, with nothing happening on a successful save.

A Technique Improvement is a boost to the cost or effectiveness of a technique. Within an Incomplete Domain, such benefits are halved. Technique Improvements are much more varied than simple Environmental Effects, so we will include a number of examples for people to use.
For example, the domain of Cursed Cannon:

normally causes three creatures within the domain to automatically suffer the effects of Granite Blast at initiative 20. Within an Incomplete Domain, this would instead allow you to make two Cursed Energy attack rolls (not affected by Improved Hit) to be made against two different creatures within the Domain. Since half of 3 is 1.5, rounded up to 2. Though if your DM decides to round down, it can be just 1.
For further examples, G Warstaff's Domain:

. This Domain normally causes all creatures within the Domain to be treated as if you have 6 seconds marked against them. In an Incomplete Domain, this would instead be having 3 seconds marked against them.
The final example, we have Ten Shadow's Domain:

. In addition to its Technique Improvements, the domain also has the Environmental Effect that causes creatures to fall into the shadows. As usual, this would be replaced with a Strength saving throw that is not affected by the Improved Hit of the Incomplete Domain. Now, for the Technique Improvements of Shadow Clones and Shikigami Clones. Shadow Clone lets you spend CE up to your CE modifier to summon a shadow clone of yourself per 1 CE spent that each have 1 HP. In an Incomplete Domain, this would instead half your output, letting you spend CE up to half your CE modifier. Shikigami Clone lets you spend the cost of a normal tamed Shikigami to summon a clone of it, which prevents your precious shikigami from dying. In an Incomplete Domain, this would function the same with the hit points of these Shikigami Clones being halved.

The ability to target and perfectly damage a creature's soul with a technique results in Soul Damage. Not all are listed, but abilities that reduce maximum hit points are treated as Soul Damage. Including, but not limited to: Soul Split Katana, Transfiguration,
. The Soul Harming ability from Soul Awareness is treated as Lesser Soul Damage. It counts as targeting the soul for effects that require it, but does not reduce maximum hit points.

. Soul Damage invalidates Reverse Cursed Technique and Regeneration, which cannot heal or remove the maximum HP reduction of Soul Damage. If Soul Damage removes a limb, it cannot be healed or regenerated.
If you want to try your hand at making your own Innate Technique, here are some guidelines to follow.

This should be the most basic application of your cursed technique or even a precursor ability. Generally, these features have a low cursed energy cost or even no cursed energy cost at all. Because of this, they are usually not directly powerful, but may scale in power as you level up.

This should be where you start gaining abilities to properly call yourself a Sorcerer. If the 1st level feature was a precursor, then this should be what you think your technique’s main abilities would be. At this level, the cursed energy cost should still be rather low so make sure to balance the feature accordingly. Generally, you want to give the feature either a base cost or have it scale depending on how cursed energy they spend. Up to their Cursed Energy modifier or Proficiency Bonus is a good way to determine output.

If your technique is based around a Domain Expansion like Deadly Sentencing or Pachinko Fever, this is the level they should get it. A Domain Expansion gained at this level usually has some kind of condition to make its sure-hit slightly weaker in exchange for gaining it at such an early level. This can include requiring cursed energy for the sure-hit effect, having a Non-Lethal Domain that has a different sure-hit effect, or having the sure-hit effect be something non-offensive.

At this level, you should gain a feature that either grants you new ways to use your technique or some kind of increase to your existing features. Whether that increase is a permanent buff or an additional effect that increases with the more cursed energy you spend.

You are approaching high level play at this level and appropriately, you should gain either your Maximum technique or a similarly strong feature. You can instead choose to have another Extension or increase to an existing feature, but unless it fits your technique, it’s probably better to have your Maximum.
Your Maximum should be one of the ultimate expressions of your technique barring your Domain Expansion and can vary from extreme burst damage to powerful buffs or debilitating debuffs.

You have finally reached the big leagues that most sorcerers die before reaching. You have finally reached the pinnacle of jujutsu allowing you to expand your domain. Generally, Domains gained at this level will be Lethal Domains with a strong sure-hit effect. Within your domain, any and all effects using your Innate Technique are guaranteed to land. Creatures automatically fail saving throws and attacks automatically hit. In addition to this, you can give your domain an additional effect such as a damaging Environmental Effect or Technique Improvement. These usually occur at initiative 20, but feel free to customize your
domain in a way that you think fits.
As an optional ruling, your DM can choose to ignore Totality, instead having all shikigami come back on a long rest, rather than being killed and eligible for Totality.
If your players find the HP cost of Rot and Blood Manipulation to be too steep, the DM can choose to reduce all HP costs to a lower amount.

Since those who are already adept at regenerating their bodies have an easier time grasping Reverse Cursed Technique, your DM can allow a character with the Blood Production feat to have an increased chance of acquiring Reverse Cursed Technique. They have advantage on any dice rolls to acquire or understand the basics of Reverse Cursed Technique.
To make Mythical Beast Amber Release more accurate, your DM can choose to instead cause the progression of stages to instead advance once stage per turn.

When a creature gains advantage from more than one source when making a skill check or attack roll, they make their roll with advantage and an additional +1 bonus for every extra source of advantage. However if the source of advantage is coming from another player taking the Help action they must describe in what way they are assisting for an attack or have proficiency in the skill to assist.
When you roll damage for a critical hit, instead of doubling the damage die you can choose to roll normally and double the entire damage roll (including modifiers or flat bonuses).

When a creature rolls a natural 1 on a saving throw against a damaging effect, they instead take critical damage. Conversely, when a creature rolls a natural 20 on a saving throw against a damaging effect, they take no damage.

A creature can choose to take a -5 penalty to an attack roll in order to specifically cripple or injure a creature. If the damage exceeds a creature’s maximum hit die + their constitution modifier, they are debilitated in a certain way depending on the GM’s interpretation or alternatively can use the Limb Damage Table. (Shooting out an eye to blind them or breaking their leg to lower their movement speed.)

When you are rolling death saving throws, you can choose to fight for your life. You gain advantage on the next death saving throw you make, but you gain 1 level of exhaustion. You can gain up to 5 levels of exhaustion this way.

As a reaction when another creature within your movement speed is targeted or hit by a harmful or damaging effect, you can move up to your movement speed towards them and take the attack in their place. However, you take twice as much damage.

As a reaction, you can choose to clash an attack or damaging effect directed at yourself. You can make a damage roll for a melee weapon attack and reduce the damage by that much. If this would reduce damage from an attack roll past 0, the attacker takes the remaining damage if they are within range. You cannot clash against psychic damage unless you have a feature that deals psychic damage.
You can clash damage this way a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus and regain all expended uses on a long rest.

You are never safe from getting double teamed. If two creatures (that are not incapacitated) are within 5 feet on opposite sides of another creature, they gain advantage on attacks against that creature. Though some DMs may choose to use +2 instead of advantage.

If a player wants to play without an Innate Technique and does not wish to use New Shadow Style or Divergent Fist, they can instead gain a +2 Ability Score Increase AND Feat they meet the prerequisites for at 1st and 3rd level. A +3 ASI and Feat at 6th level and 11th, and +3 ASI and 2 Feats at 18th level. Do be warned, this will of course be generally weaker than having a technique.

If a player would gain an ability that grants them an ability they already have, you can be a benevolent GM and let the player choose a different one. For example, if a player chooses a feat such as Incomplete Domain or Reversed Technique Prodigy, you can allow them to switch the feat out for a different feat they qualify for when they gain a feature that gives them the same or better version of that ability. Such as a Domain Expansion or Reverse Technique Understanding respectively.

If a GM wants to allow players to balance their ability scores while gaining unique features they may want, they can choose to allow players to gain an Ability Score Improvement as well as a Feat that they qualify for whenever they would gain an Ability Score Improvement.

In the main world of Jujutsu Kaisen, Tengen supports the Jujutsu world with their permanent barriers. Among the barriers that suppress cursed spirits, conceal cursed energy, and change terrain there is also the Pure Barrier that supports barrier techniques of those associated with Jujutsu High. If Tengen or a figure with similar mastery of barriers (Such as a level 20 Support Specialist) exists within your world, you can determine certain parts of your world as being within a pure barrier. Those given permission by the barrier holder only spend 1 cursed energy when casting a

A creature that is aware of the effects of the Executioner’s Sword of Deadly Sentencing can attempt desperate action to avoid instant death. A creature hit by the Executioner's Sword can use their reaction to remove one of their limbs at the point of contact to avoid death. The creature takes damage equal to the required damage to remove a limb, which cannot be reduced in any way. They suffer the penalties of missing that limb as normal.

When making a check relating to souls, you use your Soul Awareness level instead of any other ability modifiers or proficiencies. Without a level of Soul Information, you have disadvantage on any such checks
While under the effects of Technique Burnout, you gain 2 temporary levels of Reduced Output.
At 10th level, players with the Cursed Spirit race gain

to help better scale against Reverse Cursed Technique. Alternatively, the DM can allow it as a feat with a prerequisite of X level and being a Cursed Spirit race. You can use Increased Affinity as a bonus action or reaction to damage to spend up to your Cursed Energy modifier in cursed energy to regain 10 hit points per cursed energy spent. A DM should allow this for players using the Cursed Spirit races to better match up against others gaining Reverse Cursed Technique at certain levels.

In Jujutsu Kaisen, it is stated that Limitless is difficult to use without the Six Eyes due to the high cursed energy cost, making most Limitless sorcerers below average without them. If you wish to have a more canon-accurate version of the technique for NPCs or Players, increase the CE cost to activate and maintain Infinity to 3 CE for sorcerers without the Six Eyes. Double the cost of Lapse Blue, Reversal Red, Teleportation and Offensive Infinity and increase the CE cost of Hollow Purple by 5 CE.

If you want your players to be more tanky and last longer during high danger battles, DMs can choose to have player characters gain the maximum value of their hit die upon level up instead of rolling or taking average.
To make taming more difficult for early level Ten Shadows players, a DM can choose any of the following increases for untamed shikigami:
Increase the hit points by 10 x the shikigami’s CR.
Add twice the shikigami’s CR to its damage rolls.
Increase the DC of a shikigami’s feature by half its CR.
Add +2 to 1-3 ability scores of the shikigami.
For balancing purposes, DO NOT allow a player to keep these increases after completion of the taming ritual. It may seem cool or fitting, but DO NOT DO THAT.
Some optional actions that can be used by tables who want more interesting and dynamic combats.

. You gain 10 ft of additional movement that must be used to move in a straight line before hitting a target with a melee attack as part of the same action. Even if you have multiple attacks on your turn, you can only make 1 attack on this turn when using the Charge action. For every additional attack you could make, you gain a +1 to the attack roll.

. If you take the Distract action, you can attempt to Distract a creature within 15 ft of you that can see or hear you. If they are concentrating on a technique or ability, they are forced to make a concentration check to maintain the ability. Even if they succeed, your distraction increases the DC of concentration checks they make by +1 until the beginning of your turn, so long as you remain within 15 feet and continue distracting. A single creature can only be affected by up to 3 DC increases as a result of creatures using this action.

. You can attempt to sunder an item held or worn by your opponent as part of an attack action in place of a melee attack. Attempting to sunder an item provokes an attack of opportunity from the target.

If your attack is successful, you deal damage to the item normally. Damage that exceeds the object’s Hardness is subtracted from its hit points. If an object has equal to or less than half its total hit points remaining, it gains the broken condition (becomes -3 item). If the damage you deal would reduce the object to less than 0 hit points, you can choose to destroy it. If you do not choose to destroy it, the object is left with only 1 hit point and the broken condition.

. As a Full Turn Action (Action + Bonus Action + Movement), you make a melee attack while within 5 ft of an unconscious creature. The target must make a Constitution saving throw equal to the damage taken or die instantly.

The dangers of missions and school life will allow Jujutsu High students to advance by methods of self-study and intense training during the time they would advance from year to year as normal high school students. This rule is centered around that concept of progression.
When a DM wishes to invoke a Yearly Progression, a player gains one of these options:

The character may increase one ability score by 2 or increase two ability scores by 1 each, to a maximum of 20. This represents any additional training which the character subjects themselves towards to prepare for the new ‘school’ year.

The character gains a new feat which has been chosen by the player but this feat is subject to your approval. This represents new talents or traits the character has acquired to better themselves as a defender of Jujutsu society. The total number of times that a character can benefit from Yearly Progression is four times.

If your GM decides to allow players to purchase items players will likely find themselves trying to earn as much money as possible. To add a way for players to use their free time as well as opening the way for interesting RP situations, you can choose to use the following rules.

A player character can attempt to find employment. It is up to the GM to determine what jobs are available given the area your campaign is taking. A GM can use proficiencies to determine the wage of the job, depending on their modifier. If a character has a skill proficiency, tool proficiency, or even language proficiencies, that can factor into finding a job. Expertise may lead to even higher paying jobs.

A player can sometimes find a job that lets you utilize your innate technique for profit. These jobs can vary in legality depending on the GM, which may open the path for certain problems or opportunities.
If a player has Reverse Technique Prodigy or Mastered Reverse Technique, they can automatically gain $10,000 per week.

A sorcerer’s work is never done! As part of your free time, a sorcerer can dedicate themself to their work and take on more missions. Missions can be received from Jujutsu Tech, one of the Clans, and even the Government of a country. Depending on the difficulty of the job, the reward will scale accordingly.
Powerful cursed tools are extremely valuable. Their monetary worth can range from five hundred thousand to upwards of five hundred million yen. Tool Makers are always able to sell to someone.

When searching for a random cursed spirit, you can spend 1-2 hours searching the surrounding area for potential cursed spirits. Make a DC 20 Perception or Investigation check. On a failure, you can’t find any. On a success, you are able to find a cursed spirit. You must roll a d100 to decide the rarity and strength of the cursed spirit.

The most important thing when killing a sorcerer is to always kill them with cursed energy or they could come back as a cursed spirit. If you die by means lacking cursed energy while being a human sorcerer, you come back to life as a cursed spirit one week after your death. You suffer the following changes:
Your race becomes Cursed Spirit, gaining all the benefits of said race and losing all benefits of your previous one. Your race becomes a Vengeful Spirit.
You gain one Cursed Energy Feat or Innate Technique Feat of your choice that you meet the requirements of.

You lose all feats and features related to Reverse Cursed Technique. Cursed Physiology breakthrough replaced Reverse Cursed Technique Breakthrough if you possess it. For every feat lost this way you gain 2 Profane Points.

Due to your body being more resilient, your Strength, Dexterity, Constitution and CE score will increase by 2, including their maximum. However, your mind has also been affected by your transformation. Your other mental scores are reduced by 4.

When you come back to life you gain 1 level of indefinite madness. At the end of the week you must make a DC 25 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, you will gain one level of indefinite madness and must repeat the save each week. You will keep getting more indefinite madness levels on subsequent failures. On a success, you lose any madness level previously obtained and no longer make the save each week.

Object Soul Awareness is far rarer than ordinary Soul Awareness, allowing you perceive the souls of things not alive. You can only increase your Object Soul Awareness with Spiritual Teaching, but can train this alone if you have at least 6 levels of Soul Awareness
. When damaging a structure or object, your melee weapon attacks and unarmed strikes ignore damage thresholds and damage reduction.
. Melee weapon attacks and unarmed strikes deal maximum damage against objects or structures and you treat their AC as 5 lower.
. You ignore Cursed Techniques that directly increase durability of objects and gain blindsight out to 30 ft.

This is an OPTIONAL rule to reflect how different people can gain different epiphanies from achieving a breakthrough. To gain a Class Specific Understanding, you must be of the same class and have achieved at least 2 Breakthroughs. You can only gain only one Class Specific Understanding.
. When you use Cursed Reinforcement, you can instead gain 10 temporary hit points per CE spent. You can do this a number of times equal to your proficiency bonus each day.
. When you make a skill check that you are proficient with, you can treat any roll of a 9 or lower as a 10.

. You have unlocked a well of healing from deep within. You have a pool of healing separate from your RCT pool containing a number of hit points equal to twice your level. You can draw any number of healing from this pool as a bonus action to heal yourself. You can use this healing on another creature you touch at 5th level.

The aggregate amount of an individual's cursed energy isn't determined by how many negative emotions they possess but by their innate talent for jujutsu. You can use this as a standard for the cursed energy possessed by normal people or sorcerers. There are of course differences for sorcerers who are more or less talented in manipulating cursed energy and you can change this standard for your own uses.
No cursed energy; relies entirely on physical prowess or innate talent.
Minimal cursed energy, barely detectable; unaware of curses.
Temporary surge of cursed energy due to intense emotion (fear, pain, grief).
Weak cursed energy; can exorcise minor spirits or use basic techniques.
Moderate cursed energy; capable sorcerer or lesser cursed spirit.
Strong cursed energy; skilled sorcerers and mid-tier special missions.
High cursed energy; veteran sorcerers and elite-level cursed spirits.
Massive cursed energy output; national-level threat or transcendent ability.
